If all terms belong to a single cohesive area, a flat list is fine.\n31\t\n32\t## Single vs multi-context repos\n33\t\n34\t**Single context (most repos):** One `GLOSSARY.md` at the repo root.\n35\t\n36\t**Multiple contexts:** A `GLOSSARY-MAP.md` at the repo root lists the contexts, where they live, and how they relate to each other:\n37\t\n38\t```md\n39\t# Glossary Map\n40\t\n41\t## Contexts\n42\t\n43\t- [Ordering](./src/ordering/GLOSSARY.md): receives and tracks customer orders\n44\t- [Billing](./src/billing/GLOSSARY.md): generates invoices and processes payments\n45\t- [Fulfillment](./src/fulfillment/GLOSSARY.md): manages warehouse picking and shipping\n46\t\n47\t## Relationships\n48\t\n49\t- **Ordering → Fulfillment**: Ordering emits `OrderPlaced` events; Fulfillment consumes them to start picking\n50\t- **Fulfillment → Billing**: Fulfillment emits `ShipmentDispatched` events; Billing consumes them to generate invoices\n51\t- **Ordering ↔ Billing**: Shared types for `CustomerId` and `Money`\n52\t```\n53\t\n54\tThe skill infers which structure applies:\n55\t\n56\t- If `GLOSSARY-MAP.md` exists, read it to find contexts\n57\t- If only a root `GLOSSARY.md` exists, single context\n58\t- If neither exists, create a root `GLOSSARY.md` lazily when the first term is resolved\n59\t\n60\tWhen multiple contexts exist, infer which one the current topic relates to. Define what it IS, not what it does.\n- **Only include terms specific to this project's context.** General programming concepts (timeouts, error types, utility patterns) don't belong even if the project uses them extensively. Before adding a term, ask: is this a concept unique to this context, or a general programming concept? Only the former belongs.\n- **Group terms under subheadings** when natural clusters emerge. If all terms belong to a single cohesive area, a flat list is fine.\n\n## Single vs multi-context repos\n\n**Single context (most repos):** One `GLOSSARY.md` at the repo root.\n\n**Multiple contexts:** A `GLOSSARY-MAP.md` at the repo root lists the contexts, where they live, and how they relate to each other:\n\n```md\n# Glossary Map\n\n## Contexts\n\n- [Ordering](./src/ordering/GLOSSARY.md): receives and tracks customer orders\n- [Billing](./src/billing/GLOSSARY.md): generates invoices and processes payments\n- [Fulfillment](./src/fulfillment/GLOSSARY.md): manages warehouse picking and shipping\n\n## Relationships\n\n- **Ordering → Fulfillment**: Ordering emits `OrderPlaced` events; Fulfillment consumes them to start picking\n- **Fulfillment → Billing**: Fulfillment emits `ShipmentDispatched` events; Billing consumes them to generate invoices\n- **Ordering ↔ Billing**: Shared types for `CustomerId` and `Money`\n```\n\nThe skill infers which structure applies:\n\n- If `GLOSSARY-MAP.md` exists, read it to find contexts\n- If only a root `GLOSSARY.md` exists, single context\n- If neither exists, create a root `GLOSSARY.md` lazily when the first term is resolved\n\nWhen multiple contexts exist, infer which one the current topic relates to. If unclear, ask.\n","numLines":61,"startLine":1,"totalLines":61}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"aaf2414b-9606-411b-8363-423b6a8aa538","session_id":"4b1a37e3-ea11-48e9-baa9-b66b752b7a0d","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/faisa/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"6e0298fd-6441-4373-ab13-28afb21c8981","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"716bac6c-1704-4a30-bbfd-ac9b15848fa8","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011CfmgmoRZikCP9iKSo7zZp","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01S3CqMxnZYZqzYWqZqxS1Fq","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/faisa/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/CONTEXT.md","content":"# CONTEXT.md glossary\n\nThe Chi Chapter of Delta Tau Delta at Kenyon College runs a small CMS: officers write content locally, and the president releases it to a public static site for prospective members, alumni, parents and Kenyon staff.\n\n## Language\n\n### People\n\n**Officer**:\nA chapter member who holds a position (president, secretary, social media chair, and so on) for a term. Officers change about once a year.\n_Avoid_: Staff, member (a member need not hold a position)\n\n**User**:\nAn Officer's login account in the CMS.\n_Avoid_: Account, profile\n\n**Admin**:\nThe role held by the president. Controls Users, Pages, navigation, and the final release to the public site.\n_Avoid_: Superuser, owner\n\n**Editor**:\nThe role held by the other Officers (secretary, social media chairs, alumni relations chair, community service chair). Writes their own Posts and edits Pages assigned to them.\n_Avoid_: Contributor, author (author is a Post's creator, not a role)\n\n**Deactivated**:\nA User who can no longer log in. Their content and byline stay; the account is never deleted.\n_Avoid_: Deleted, disabled, banned\n\n**Term**:\nThe title and academic year an Officer served, such as \"Secretary, 2026–27\".\n_Avoid_: Position, tenure\n\n**Byline**:\nThe public attribution on a Post: the author's full name, title, and Term.\n_Avoid_: Credit, author line\n\n### Content\n\n**Post**:\nA dated news item written by one Editor or the Admin, listed in the public news feed.\n_Avoid_: Article, update, entry\n\n**Page**:\nAn undated, authorless piece of standing content (About, History, Community Service) that can appear in public navigation.\n_Avoid_: Section\n\n**Assigned editor**:\nThe one Editor, besides the Admin, who may edit a given Page.\n_Avoid_: Page owner\n\n**Draft**:\nContent that has not been marked Published. Never leaves the database.\n_Avoid_: Unpublished (ambiguous with unpublishing something that was live)\n\n**Published**:\nThe status an Editor or Admin gives content to say it is ready to go public. {"parentUuid":"481643b2-1575-4c61-8ee5-8b134bd80c34","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfmgnap5Q88i6wZkBWmi2","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Q1 to Q7 are settled, and I added them to `CONTEXT.md`. That covers Officer, User, Admin, Editor, Deactivated, Term, Byline, Post, Page, Assigned editor, Draft, Published, Live, Publish run, Navigation and Slug. I split \"Published\" (what an editor sets) from \"Live\" (what is actually on the site), so Q4's two gates have separate names.\n\n## Q8: images — I recommend (b), the admin-managed folder\n\n- **Safer:** real uploads mean validating file type, size and filenames, blocking SVG (which can carry script), and stripping EXIF data. Phone photos carry GPS location, which is exactly the \"personal info\" you said must not go public. Stripping it means re-encoding images with Pillow, which isn't in `pyproject.toml`. `CLAUDE.md` says to ask before adding a dependency, so I'm asking you now.\n- **Simpler:** with (b), you add the file to the folder yourself and editors reference it with `![alt text](img/name.jpg)`. There is no upload form and no new dependency.\n- **Publish behaviour:** a Publish run copies only the images that Published content references. A photo that only a Draft uses never reaches `site/`, which keeps the rule that drafts never leave the database.\n- **Cost:** you become the one who adds photos. That cuts against what you said about not being the only one who can make changes. You can offset it by letting editors hand you photos, since you review everything before a Publish run anyway.\n- **Rider:** photos in the repo folder get committed. If the GitHub repo is public, they are public the moment you push, even before a Publish run. Keep unreleased photos out of the folder until they're approved.\n\nIf you want editors to upload themselves, the honest route is (b) now and uploads later. Uploads would add Pillow plus the checks above, and I'd record that as a stretch goal.\n\n## Round 2\n\n❓ **Q9** - **Can an Assigned editor delete a Page or publish it?**: Q1 says they can edit it. Two follow-ups:\n- Can they delete it?\n- Can they set its status to Published, as editors can with Posts?\n\n➡️ No delete, so only the Admin deletes Pages. Yes to setting Published, because your Q4 rule already gives you the final gate in the Publish run. The Admin alone creates Pages, picks the Assigned editor, and controls `show_in_nav` and nav order.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q10** - **What happens to a Page when its Assigned editor is Deactivated or reassigned?**: Turnover happens every year, and the Assigned editor is a person, not a title.\n- When a User is Deactivated, their Pages become unassigned and Admin-only until you reassign them.\n- Is it simpler to assign a Page to a *position* so the next holder inherits it?\n\n➡️ Assign to the User. When that User is Deactivated, the Page is left unassigned and the user list warns you (\"2 pages need a new editor\"). Position-based assignment needs an Officer-position model that nothing else needs.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q11** - **Is the Byline's Term live or a snapshot?**: Say the social chair writes a post as \"Social Chair, 2026–27\". Next year that User is deactivated, or their title changes.\n- (a) The Byline reads the User's current title and Term, so old posts change when the User record changes.\n- (b) The title and Term are copied onto the Post when it is first marked Published, so each post keeps what was true then.\n\n➡️ (b). Your Term-year idea only works if old posts don't change. Editing a User's title later must not rewrite history.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q12** - **Who can read what in the content list?**: Your notes say the status column was hard to see, and that you weren't sure editors should see everyone's posts. Under Q1, Editors can only edit their own.\n- (a) Editors see only their own Posts, plus Pages assigned to them.\n- (b) Editors see everything but the other items are read-only. Admin sees and filters everything.\n\n➡️ (b). Officers should know what the others have posted so they don't duplicate it, and read-only rows remove the clutter risk you raised. Filters are status, type (Post or Page) and author, with a \"Mine\" shortcut. Status is a large coloured badge. There are no categories, tags or bulk actions.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q13** - **What does the dashboard show?**: Candidates are:\n- Counts of Drafts and Published items.\n- \"Pending release\": Published items that aren't Live yet, or changed since the last Publish run.\n- Pages that need a new editor.\n- Your own recent items.\n- A button to jump to the editor, with the same view for both roles apart from Admin-only widgets.\n\n➡️ Show \"Pending release\" first, since it is the one number you act on, then Drafts waiting, then your own recent items. Pages needing an editor appears for the Admin only. No charts.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q14** - **How should Preview behave?**: Your WordPress note says the preview button was hard to find, and that a draft didn't show on the site.\n- The Preview button sits right next to Save.\n- Preview renders the exact sanitized HTML that a Publish run would produce, with the real Byline and navigation.\n- Preview is visible only to logged-in users.\n- Should it open beside the editor or on its own page? Live-while-typing costs more under ADR-002.\n\n➡️ A prominent \"Preview\" button next to Save, which renders the same sanitize-then-render code that `cms publish` uses. It opens in a new tab with a \"Draft preview, not public\" banner. It updates on click, not as you type, which is the trade ADR-002 already accepts.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q15** - **When an Editor hits a permission wall, what do they see?**: In your test the editor got \"You need a higher level of permission\" and no way to know who the admin is.\n- Show a friendly message naming the current Admin's display name and an email or contact line.\n- Is the Admin's contact allowed to appear inside the console? It stays out of the public site.\n\n➡️ Yes. Hide controls an Editor can't use, and show a short message naming the current Admin and their chapter email if they navigate there directly. The contact lives in an Admin-set setting and never appears in `site/`.\n\n---\n\nAnswer Q9 to Q15 however is quickest. Round 3 will cover the points still open: what Home shows, how many posts the news feed lists, how login and sessions behave (lockout, password reset when no email server exists), and what CSRF and first-run setup look like for a brand-new Admin."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1442,"cache_read_input_tokens":53937,"output_tokens":2161,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1442,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":2161,"cache_read_input_tokens":53937,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1442,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1442},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"serverClassifierRequest":"16657ee8-3f88-4eaa-bb0f-3fceafb9029e","apiBlockIndex":0,"requestId":"req_011CfmgnaVU5oRLHDYr1ZhD6","type":"assistant","uuid":"109c7ed7-8dee-4b44-83d5-4184784b36e3","timestamp":"2026-10-06T21:23:38.359Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"4b1a37e3-ea11-48e9-baa9-b66b752b7a0d","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/faisa/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"6e0298fd-6441-4373-ab13-28afb21c8981","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

Officers change about once a year.\n_Avoid_: Staff, member (a member need not hold a position)\n\n**User**:\nAn Officer's login account in the CMS.\n_Avoid_: Account, profile\n\n**Admin**:\nThe role held by the president. Controls Users, Pages, navigation, and the final release to the public site.\n_Avoid_: Superuser, owner\n\n**Editor**:\nThe role held by the other Officers (secretary, social media chairs, alumni relations chair, community service chair). Writes their own Posts and edits Pages assigned to them.\n_Avoid_: Contributor, author (author is a Post's creator, not a role)\n\n**Deactivated**:\nA User who can no longer log in. Their content and byline stay; the account is never deleted.\n_Avoid_: Deleted, disabled, banned\n\n**Term**:\nThe title and academic year an Officer served, such as \"Secretary, 2026–27\".\n_Avoid_: Position, tenure\n\n**Byline**:\nThe public attribution on a Post: the author's full name, title, and Term.\n_Avoid_: Credit, author line\n\n### Content\n\n**Post**:\nA dated news item written by one Editor or the Admin, listed in the public news feed.\n_Avoid_: Article, update, entry\n\n**Page**:\nAn undated, authorless piece of standing content (About, History, Community Service) that can appear in public navigation.\n_Avoid_: Section\n\n**Assigned editor**:\nThe one Editor, besides the Admin, who may edit a given Page.\n_Avoid_: Page owner\n\n**Draft**:\nContent that has not been marked Published. Never leaves the database.\n_Avoid_: Unpublished (ambiguous with unpublishing something that was live)\n\n**Published**:\nThe status an Editor or Admin gives content to say it is ready to go public. It does not make the content Live.\n_Avoid_: Live, released\n\n**Live**:\nPresent on the public site as of the latest Publish run.\n_Avoid_: Deployed, online\n\n**Publish run**:\nThe Admin's `cms publish` step. It shows what will change, asks for confirmation, then renders all Published content to the static site.\n_Avoid_: Deploy, release, export\n\n**Navigation**:\nThe public site's top links: Home, the Pages marked to show in navigation in the Admin's chosen order, then News.\n_Avoid_: Menu\n\n**Slug**:\nThe URL-safe name of a Post or Page, unique within its kind and locked after first being Published.\n_Avoid_: Permalink, URL name\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":64,"oldLines":6,"newStart":64,"newLines":10,"lines":[" The Admin's `cms publish` step. {"parentUuid":"fc6c0825-f259-4be0-bdf0-c6f4b0ac1153","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfmh7FNJfb2tWzDfL2AyX","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Q8 through Q15 are settled. I added **Pending release** to `CONTEXT.md` and updated **Byline** to say it is fixed at first publish (Q11). I did not write an ADR for any of these. They follow from ADR-001 or are easy to reverse, so none meets the bar.\n\nWhat's settled so far:\n- **Images:** you add them to an admin-managed folder, and uploads are the stretch goal.\n- **Pages:** an Assigned editor can edit and mark Published but can't delete. When their account is Deactivated, the Page becomes unassigned, and the user list warns you.\n- **Byline:** the title and Term are fixed when a Post is first marked Published.\n- **Content list:** Editors can see everything but only edit their own. The status badge is large, with no categories, tags or bulk actions.\n- **Dashboard, Preview and permission message:** all as I proposed.\n\n## Round 3\n\n❓ **Q16** - **What happens when someone edits an item that is already Live?**: Your \"half-written draft goes public\" fear has a back door. Suppose the secretary edits a Live Post and saves halfway. The database now holds the half-edit, and your next Publish run would put it on the site.\n- (a) Editing a Published item changes it in place. The Publish run summary shows it as \"changed\", and your confirmation is the only gate.\n- (b) Editing a Published item flips it back to Draft. It stays Live with the old text until a Publish run, then drops off the site if it wasn't re-marked Published.\n- (c) Keep a separate draft copy of the edit.\n\n➡️ (a), with a clear \"changed since last release\" marker in the content list. (b) makes edits accidentally take pages down, and (c) is a revision system, which is too much for this project. The summary should show the changed items by title, so a half-edit is easy to spot before you confirm.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q17** - **Do Posts need an event date?**: The brief's example is a rush announcement with the wrong date. Your required fields are `title`, `slug`, `body`, status, author and timestamps (created, updated, published). None of them is \"the date of the event\".\n- (a) No event date field. The editor writes the date in the body, and Preview shows it.\n- (b) An optional `event_date` field, shown on the post and in the news feed.\n\n➡️ (a). The \"wrong date\" problem is a typing mistake, and Preview plus your final approval catch it. A date field adds a second date that could also be wrong. The public date shown on a Post is the published date.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q18** - **What do Home and the news feed show?**: The site is static, so every list is rendered at publish time.\n- Home: a short chapter blurb (an Admin-edited Page, such as \"Home\") plus the latest N Posts?\n- News: all Posts newest-first, or paginated?\n- Does a Post show the full body in the list, or a title, date and excerpt?\n\n➡️ Home is a normal Page flagged as the home page, followed by the 5 latest Posts as title, date and the first paragraph. The News page lists every Post newest-first, with titles and dates only, on one page for now. A year of chapter posts is a short list, so pagination isn't worth building yet.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q19** - **How do login, sessions and password recovery work?**: There's no email server and the console is local. Settle these together:\n- Password reset: only the Admin sets a temporary password for another User, who must change it at next login. For the Admin's own forgotten password, the answer is a command-line reset on the machine.\n- Failed logins: slow or lock after N tries?\n- How long does a session last: until the browser closes, or a fixed time like 8 hours?\n- Password rules: minimum length only?\n\n➡️ The Admin resets Editors' passwords and a temp password forces a change at next login. The Admin's own recovery is `cms reset-password <username>` on the machine. Lock a username for 10 minutes after 5 failed logins. Sessions last 8 hours and are cut at once on Deactivation (Q3). Passwords need at least 12 characters and no other rules. Passwords are argon2-hashed and never logged.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q20** - **How does the first Admin get created, and what survives the handover?**: Your old site's problem was one person who never updated it. The new bus-factor risk is that the database and repo live on one machine. The `.db` file is gitignored, so Git isn't a backup.\n- First run: `cms create-admin` prompts for a name and password, with no default password in the code or the seed script.\n- Handover: the next president needs the repo, the database, the image folder and a one-page checklist.\n- Backup: should there be a `cms backup` that copies the database to a dated file you can store somewhere private?\n\n➡️ `cms create-admin` with a hidden password prompt. A `cms backup` command that writes a timestamped copy of the database outside the repo folder, plus a handover checklist in the README. Backup files are not committed. This is cheap, and it directly answers \"what if the president graduates\".\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q21** - **What does `cms publish` do from start to finish?**: `ghp-import` can push `site/` to the `gh-pages` branch. Options for the flow:\n- (a) One command: render, show the summary (new, changed, removed), ask \"publish? y/N\", then push.\n- (b) Render only, and you push separately.\n- Is the repo public? That decides whether committed photos (Q8's rider) are public before a Publish run.\n\n➡️ (a). It's one command, and the confirmation matches the final approval you asked for. It refuses to push if the render fails or any Draft would appear in the output. Treat the repo as public unless you tell me it's private, and keep unreleased photos out of the folder.\n\n---\n\nAnswer Q16 to Q21 however is quickest (\"yes to all\" is fine, or name the ones you want changed). Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"posts/x.html\"), never\n     root-absolute (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport shutil\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape\n\nfrom app import settings\n\nCSS = \"\"\"/* Minimal starter styles — make them yours. */\n:root { color-scheme: light dark; }\nbody { font: 16px/1.6 system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 42rem; padding: 1rem; }\nheader a { font-weight: 700; text-decoration: none; }\nmain { margin-block: 2rem; }\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef environment() -> Environment:\n    return Environment(\n        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n        autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]),\n    )\n\n\ndef render_site(out: Path | None = None) -> Path:\n    out = out or settings.SITE\n    if out.exists():\n        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    out.mkdir(parents=True)\n    env = environment()\n    (out / \"style.css\").write_text(CSS)\n    (out / \"index.html\").write_text(\n        env.get_template(\"public/home.html\").render(\n            title=settings.SITE_TITLE, items=[], css_path=\"style.css\",\n            home_path=\"index.html\",\n        )\n    )\n    return out\n","numLines":48,"startLine":1,"totalLines":48}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"759eedf5-5318-414d-8e9f-90c30cb9ec5a","session_id":"4b1a37e3-ea11-48e9-baa9-b66b752b7a0d","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/faisa/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"6e0298fd-6441-4373-ab13-28afb21c8981","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

It renders all Published content to the local static site, shows what is new, changed or removed, and refuses if any Draft would appear.\n_Avoid_: Export, build\n\n**Deploy**:\nThe Admin's `cms deploy` step. After the Admin confirms, it pushes the rendered static site to the public host, making its content Live.\n_Avoid_: Release, push, upload\n\n**Pending release**:\nPublished content that is not yet Live, or that has changed since the last Deploy.\n_Avoid_: Queued, staged","originalFile":"# CONTEXT.md glossary\n\nThe Chi Chapter of Delta Tau Delta at Kenyon College runs a small CMS: officers write content locally, and the president releases it to a public static site for prospective members, alumni, parents and Kenyon staff.\n\n## Language\n\n### People\n\n**Officer**:\nA chapter member who holds a position (president, secretary, social media chair, and so on) for a term. Officers change about once a year.\n_Avoid_: Staff, member (a member need not hold a position)\n\n**User**:\nAn Officer's login account in the CMS.\n_Avoid_: Account, profile\n\n**Admin**:\nThe role held by the president. Controls Users, Pages, navigation, and the final release to the public site.\n_Avoid_: Superuser, owner\n\n**Editor**:\nThe role held by the other Officers (secretary, social media chairs, alumni relations chair, community service chair). Writes their own Posts and edits Pages assigned to them.\n_Avoid_: Contributor, author (author is a Post's creator, not a role)\n\n**Deactivated**:\nA User who can no longer log in. Their content and byline stay; the account is never deleted.\n_Avoid_: Deleted, disabled, banned\n\n**Term**:\nThe title and academic year an Officer served, such as \"Secretary, 2026–27\".\n_Avoid_: Position, tenure\n\n**Byline**:\nThe public attribution on a Post: the author's full name, title, and Term, fixed when the Post is first marked Published.\n_Avoid_: Credit, author line\n\n### Content\n\n**Post**:\nA dated news item written by one Editor or the Admin, listed in the public news feed.\n_Avoid_: Article, update, entry\n\n**Page**:\nAn undated, authorless piece of standing content (About, History, Community Service) that can appear in public navigation.\n_Avoid_: Section\n\n**Assigned editor**:\nThe one Editor, besides the Admin, who may edit a given Page.\n_Avoid_: Page owner\n\n**Draft**:\nContent that has not been marked Published. Never leaves the database.\n_Avoid_: Unpublished (ambiguous with unpublishing something that was live)\n\n**Published**:\nThe status an Editor or Admin gives content to say it is ready to go public. It does not make the content Live.\n_Avoid_: Live, released\n\n**Live**:\nPresent on the public site as of the latest Publish run.\n_Avoid_: Deployed, online\n\n**Publish run**:\nThe Admin's `cms publish` step. It shows what will change, asks for confirmation, then renders all Published content to the static site.\n_Avoid_: Deploy, release, export\n\n**Pending release**:\nPublished content that is not yet Live, or that has changed since the last Publish run.\n_Avoid_: Queued, staged\n\n**Navigation**:\nThe public site's top links: Home, the Pages marked to show in navigation in the Admin's chosen order, then News.\n_Avoid_: Menu\n\n**Slug**:\nThe URL-safe name of a Post or Page, unique within its kind and locked after first being Published.\n_Avoid_: Permalink, URL name\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":57,"oldLines":15,"newStart":57,"newLines":19,"lines":[" _Avoid_: Live, released"," "," **Live**:","-Present on the public site as of the latest Publish run.","-_Avoid_: Deployed, online","+Present on the public site as of the latest Deploy.","+_Avoid_: Online, released"," "," **Publish run**:","-The Admin's `cms publish` step. {"parentUuid":"643bc8c6-c4ac-4876-b7c0-c710a5ad05a2","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011CfmhWpRnkXnBEhxPRohP3","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I've updated `CONTEXT.md`. **Live** now means \"as of the latest Deploy\", there's a new **Deploy** term, and **Publish run** is now render-and-check only.\n\nYou were right about Q21, and I'd muddled it. The scaffold already splits the two commands: `app/cli.py` has `publish` and `deploy` as separate subcommands, so I'm keeping that split. `publish` renders and shows the summary, and `deploy` pushes `site/` to `gh-pages`. The deploy confirmation is your final approval.\n\n## Recap for you to confirm\n\n**Roles and permissions**\n- **Admin (president):**\n  - Controls Users, Pages, navigation (order and show/hide), page assignments, password resets, `publish` and `deploy`.\n  - The last active Admin can't be deactivated or demoted.\n- **Editors:**\n  - Create and edit their own Posts, and see all content read-only.\n  - Edit only their Assigned Pages, and mark them Published. They can't delete Pages or published Posts, and can delete only their own Drafts.\n- **Deactivation:**\n  - Accounts are Deactivated, never deleted, and the lockout is immediate.\n  - Posts and bylines stay.\n  - The Admin sees a warning when Pages lose their editor and need reassigning.\n\n**Content**\n- **Posts:** `title`, `slug`, Markdown body, Draft/Published, author, and created, updated and published timestamps. They also have an **optional event date** (Q17).\n- **Byline:** full name, title and Term, copied when the Post is first marked Published.\n- **Pages:**\n  - Pages are undated and authorless, with Draft/Published, `nav_order` and `show_in_nav`.\n  - One Page is flagged as Home.\n  - Navigation is Home, then the Pages in order, then News.\n- **Slugs:** generated from the title, unique, locked after first Published, with only the Admin able to unlock.\n- **Markdown:**\n  - Basic formatting and links are allowed, and raw HTML is stripped.\n  - Images are allowed only from the admin-managed folder, referenced by relative path.\n  - Only referenced, Published images are copied to `site/`.\n  - You add the photos yourself, and unapproved ones stay out of the folder, since the repo is public.\n\n**Workflow**\n- Editors work on a machine that runs the console, such as a shared chapter laptop. Remote editor access is the stretch goal.\n- Editing a Live item changes it in place, and your review of the summary is the gate.\n- **`cms publish`:** renders `site/`, shows new, changed and removed items, and refuses if a Draft would appear.\n- **`cms deploy`:** asks you to confirm, then pushes to `gh-pages`.\n\n**Console and accounts**\n- The dashboard leads with Pending release.\n- The content list has status, type and author filters, a \"Mine\" shortcut and a big status badge. It has no categories, tags or bulk actions.\n- Preview sits next to Save, uses the same render-and-sanitize code, and shows a \"not public\" banner. It refreshes on click, not as you type.\n- A blocked Editor sees a message naming the Admin and their contact line, which never reaches `site/`.\n- **Login and accounts:** `cms create-admin` creates the first Admin with a hidden password prompt. `cms backup` writes the database outside the repo. A handover checklist goes in the README.\n- **Sessions:**\n  - 12-character minimum passwords, hashed with argon2, never logged.\n  - 5 failed logins lock the username for 10 minutes.\n  - Sessions last 8 hours.\n  - Temporary passwords force a change.\n\n## Defaults I'm assuming because of your latest answers\n\nThese weren't asked, so veto any of them.\n1. A Post with an event date shows both its published date and \"Event: <date>\". The News feed is still sorted by published date, not event date.\n2. \"Changed since last Deploy\" needs a baseline, so a successful `cms deploy` records a fingerprint of each item. The `publish` summary compares against that.\n3. `cms deploy` warns and stops if content has changed since the last `cms publish`, so stale files in `site/` can't be pushed by accident.\n4. The glossary uses \"Publish run\" and \"Deploy\" as defined above. \"Published\" means ready for release, and \"Live\" means actually on the site.\n\nIf this matches what you meant, say \"confirmed\" and I'll consider the grilling done. If anything is off, tell me which line and I'll go back to it."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1386,"cache_read_input_tokens":63600,"output_tokens":1498,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1386,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1498,"cache_read_input_tokens":63600,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1386,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1386},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"serverClassifierRequest":"f0dad5f0-cd20-4d04-9c0a-319d21409822","apiBlockIndex":0,"requestId":"req_011CfmhWowHE3PYCusbkmCwi","type":"assistant","uuid":"01ed3b1e-209a-4da1-9ddf-f41270b9b04d","timestamp":"2026-10-06T21:33:04.311Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"4b1a37e3-ea11-48e9-baa9-b66b752b7a0d","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/faisa/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"6e0298fd-6441-4373-ab13-28afb21c8981","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

These five extras are the LAST tickets, so the user can cut them if time runs out: (1) images from the admin-managed folder, (2) optional post event date, (3) `cms backup`, (4) login lockout (5 fails, 10 min), (5) deploy fingerprints (baseline for \"changed since last deploy\" and the stale-site warning in `cms deploy`).\n\n**Why:** The user is a student on a two-week deadline and wants to drop extras without breaking required work. The grader expects the 7 capabilities.\n\n**How to apply:** Put the extras after the 7 core tickets, each independent of the others and of the core. The core must work without them: Markdown sanitizer strips images, the `cms publish` summary falls back to listing all Published items, and login works without lockout. Each user story should be in the format of:\n\n1. As an <actor>, I want a <feature>, so that <benefit>\n\n<user-story-example>\n1. As a mobile bank customer, I want to see balance on my accounts, so that I can make better informed decisions about my spending\n</user-story-example>\n\nThis list of user stories should be extremely extensive and cover all aspects of the feature.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\nA list of implementation decisions that were made. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.\n\n## Conventions\n\n- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title \"...\" --body \"...\"`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.\n- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.\n- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.\n- **Make an issue a sub-issue of a parent**: `gh issue create --parent <parent> ...`, or `gh issue edit <parent> --add-sub-issue <child>` afterwards (`gh` 2.94+). Older `gh`: `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<parent>/sub_issues -F sub_issue_id=<child-db-id>` (database id, as in **Blocking** below). Without sub-issues, put `Part of #<parent>` at the top of the child body.\n- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body \"...\"`\n- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label \"...\"` / `--remove-label \"...\"`\n- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment \"...\"`\n\nInfer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.\n\n## Pull requests as a triage surface\n\n**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_\n\nWhen set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:\n\n- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.\n- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh api --paginate 'repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls?state=open' --jq '.[] | select(.author_association | IN(\"OWNER\",\"MEMBER\",\"COLLABORATOR\") | not) | {number, title, author: .user.login, author_association, labels: [.labels[].name]}'`.\n- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.\n\nGitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either: resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.\n\n## When a skill says \"publish to the issue tracker\"\n\nCreate a GitHub issue.\n\n## When a skill says \"fetch the relevant ticket\"\n\nRun `gh issue view <number> --comments`.\n\n## Wayfinding operations\n\nUsed by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.\n\n- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.\n- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (see **Make an issue a sub-issue of a parent**). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.\n- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies**, the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). GitHub reports `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only, the live gate). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.\n- **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (`issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0`, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.\n- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me`, the session's first write.\n- **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body \"<answer>\"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.\n# Triage Labels\n\nThe skills speak in terms of five canonical triage roles. {"parentUuid":"780530eb-34f2-4186-9a51-bac847d04016","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011CfmhvgGabko8ingVjzqed","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01YTfCAYRrre6q2edVPzDJp4","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/tmp/claude-1000/-home-faisa-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/6e0298fd-6441-4373-ab13-28afb21c8981/scratchpad/spec.md","content":"## Problem Statement\n\nThe Chi Chapter of Delta Tau Delta at Kenyon College has an outdated website run by one alum who never updates it. Alumni cannot find updates, information is spread out, and active Officers cannot change anything. Prospective members, alumni, parents and Kenyon staff want to learn about the chapter's members, news, community service and history.\n\nThe chapter president needs a site that the Officers themselves can keep current, with these things never happening:\n\n- A graduated Officer can still log in and post.\n- An Editor deletes or changes the chapter history Page, or another Officer's Post.\n- A half-written Draft goes public, such as a rush announcement with the wrong date.\n- Members' personal information ends up public.\n\nThe people running it are college students who are comfortable with computers but not technical, and their roles change hands about once a year.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small CMS in which the president (Admin) and the other Officers (Editors) write Posts and Pages in a local admin console. The Admin runs `cms publish` to render the Published content into a static site, then `cms deploy` to push it to GitHub Pages after confirming. Nothing is Live until the Admin has reviewed and deployed it.\n\nThe console is deliberately plain. It has a dashboard that leads with what is waiting for release, a content list with a large status badge and only the filters that matter, and an editor with a prominent Preview. An Editor can only change their own Posts and the Pages the Admin has assigned to them. Officers who graduate are Deactivated immediately, and their past work and Byline stay.\n\nThe admin console never goes on the public internet (ADR-001). Editors work on a machine that runs the console, such as a shared chapter-house laptop.\n\n### The 7 required capabilities, for this client\n\n1. **Login with hashed passwords.** An Officer logs in with their email and password. Passwords are stored only as argon2 hashes. A wrong password gets a generic refusal that does not reveal whether the email exists. The Admin sets a temporary password for another User, who must change it at next login. The Admin's own recovery is a command on the machine.\n2. **Two roles, Admin and Editor.** The president is the Admin. Every other Officer is an Editor who writes their own Posts and edits only the Pages the Admin assigned to them. Access is enforced in code on every request, not by hiding links.\n3. **Posts.** Title, Slug, Markdown body, Draft or Published, author, and created, updated and published timestamps. Each Post shows a Byline with the author's full name, title and Term, fixed when the Post is first marked Published.\n4. **Pages in public Navigation.** Standing content such as About, History and Community Service has no author and no date. The Admin creates Pages, assigns one Editor to each, and chooses which appear in Navigation and in what order. One Page is the Home page.\n5. **Admin console.** A dashboard, a filterable content list, and an editor with Markdown Preview.\n6. **Admin-only user management with Deactivation.** The Admin creates Users, sets a role, title and Term, resets passwords, and Deactivates Users when they leave office. Deactivated Users are never deleted and cannot log in, even with an old session.\n7. **Static public site via `cms publish`.** `cms publish` renders only Published content into the static site, with sanitized Markdown and relative paths only. It shows what is new, changed or removed, and refuses if any Draft would appear. `cms deploy` is a separate command that confirms with the Admin before pushing to GitHub Pages.\n\n## User Stories\n\n### Login and accounts\n\n1. As an Officer, I want to log in with my email and password, so that I can reach the console without a separate username.\n2. As an Officer, I want to log out, so that the next person on a shared chapter laptop cannot use my account.\n3. As an Officer who typed a wrong password, I want a clear refusal that does not say whether my email exists, so that nobody can use the login form to find out who has an account.\n4. As an Officer who was just given a temporary password, I want to be made to choose my own at first login, so that the Admin never knows my real password.\n5. As an Officer choosing a password, I want to be told the minimum length, so that I do not guess at hidden rules.\n6. As the Admin, I want a session to end after 8 hours, so that a logged-in shared laptop does not stay open overnight.\n7. As the Admin, I want passwords stored only as argon2 hashes and never logged, so that a copied database does not expose anyone's password.\n8. As the Admin who forgot my own password, I want a command on the machine to reset it, so that I am not locked out when no email server exists.\n9. As the Admin setting up the CMS for the first time, I want `cms create-admin` to ask for my email and a hidden password, so that there is no default password in the code or the demo data.\n10. As an Admin, I want an anonymous visitor to be redirected to login on every admin URL, so that no admin content is ever shown to someone who is not logged in.\n\n### Roles and permissions\n\n11. As an Editor, I want to create Posts and edit only my own, so that I can do my job without being able to damage another Officer's work.\n12. As an Editor, I want to see every Post and Page in the content list but have other people's rows read-only, so that I know what is already written without being able to change it.\n13. As an Editor, I want to edit a Page the Admin assigned to me, so that I can keep my area (for example Community Service or History) current without needing the president.\n14. As an Editor, I want other Editors to be unable to edit my Assigned Page, so that my work is not overwritten by someone else.\n15. As an Editor, I want to mark my own Posts and my Assigned Pages Published, so that I am not waiting on the president for every step.\n16. As an Editor, I want to set my own Post back to Draft, so that I can take something down that I got wrong.\n17. As an Editor, I want to delete my own Drafts, so that I can clean up abandoned writing.\n18. As an Editor who tries to reach a page I am not allowed to use, I want a short message naming the current Admin and how to reach them, so that I know who to ask for higher permission.\n19. As an Editor, I want controls I cannot use to be hidden, so that the console is not cluttered with buttons that do nothing.\n20. As the Admin, I want an Editor who requests an admin-only URL directly to be refused (403 or redirect), so that hiding links is never the only protection.\n21. As the Admin, I want to edit and delete any Post or Page, so that I can correct problems when an Officer is unavailable.\n22. As the Admin, I want a deleted-Post rule that lets Editors delete only Drafts, so that a published announcement cannot be erased in one click.\n\n### Posts\n\n23. As an Editor, I want to write a Post with a title and a Markdown body, so that I can post news without knowing HTML.\n24. As an Editor, I want the Slug to be filled in from the title and editable until the Post is first Published, so that URLs are readable and I can fix awkward ones.\n25. As an Editor, I want a clear error if my Slug is already used by another Post, so that two Posts never share a URL.\n26. As a reader following a shared link, I want a Post's URL to stay the same after it is Published, so that links from alumni emails and social media do not break.\n27. As the Admin, I want to unlock a Slug after first publish when a correction is needed, so that the lock protects links but is not permanent.\n28. As an Editor, I want the Post to record who wrote it and when it was created, updated and published, so that readers and Officers can see its history.\n29. As a reader, I want each Post to show its author's full name, title and Term, so that I know who at the chapter is speaking and in which year.\n30. As an Editor, I want the Byline to be fixed when the Post is first Published, so that old Posts do not change when someone's title or Term later changes.\n31. As an Editor, I want to edit a Published Post in place and have the change reach the site at the next release, so that I can fix a typo without taking the Post down first.\n32. As an Editor, I want Posts that changed since the last Deploy to be marked in the content list, so that I can see which edits are not yet Live.\n\n### Pages and Navigation\n\n33. As the Admin, I want to create a Page and assign it to one Editor, so that every standing area of the site has a named maintainer.\n34. As the Admin, I want to choose which Pages appear in Navigation and their order, so that visitors see About, History and Community Service in a sensible order.\n35. As a visitor, I want the top of every public page to show Home, the chapter's Pages, and News, so that I can find things from anywhere.\n36. As a visitor, I want a Published Page without a Navigation entry to still be reachable by its URL, so that unlisted pages such as a rush information page can be shared directly.\n37. As the Admin, I want one Page flagged as the Home page, so that the site's front door is under my control.\n38. As the Admin, I want only the Admin to be able to delete a Page, so that an Editor cannot remove the chapter history Page.\n39. As the Admin, I want Pages to have no author and no date on the public site, so that standing content reads as the chapter's own voice.\n40. As the Admin, I want Pages whose Assigned editor was Deactivated to be left unassigned and Admin-only, so that nobody inherits access by accident.\n\n### Admin console\n\n41. As an Officer, I want a dashboard that leads with Pending release, so that I see first what is waiting to go public.\n42. As an Officer, I want the dashboard to show Drafts waiting and my own recent items, so that I can pick up where I left off.\n43. As the Admin, I want the dashboard to show Pages needing a new Assigned editor, so that turnover problems are visible.\n44. As an Officer, I want a content list with a large, clearly coloured status badge for Draft and Published, so that I can tell the status at a glance.\n45. As an Officer, I want to filter the content list by status, by type (Post or Page) and by author, so that I can find things quickly.\n46. As an Officer, I want a \"Mine\" shortcut on the content list, so that I can see only my own work in one click.\n47. As an Officer, I want the content list to have no categories, tags or bulk actions, so that it makes sense without a technical background.\n48. As an Editor, I want a Preview button right next to Save, so that I do not have to hunt for it.\n49. As an Editor, I want Preview to render the exact sanitized HTML that the Publish run would write, with the real Byline and Navigation, so that what I check is what visitors will see.\n50. As an Editor, I want Preview to say clearly that it is a draft preview and not public, so that I never confuse it with the live site.\n51. As an Editor, I want to see Markdown I typed with a script or event handler stripped in Preview, so that I find out about unsafe content before it is published.\n\n### User management\n\n52. As the Admin, I want to create a User with an email, display name, title, Term and role, so that a new Officer can start work.\n53. As the Admin, I want to change a User's role, title and Term, so that the console follows who currently holds each position.\n54. As the Admin, I want to Deactivate a User when they leave office, so that a graduated Officer can no longer log in or post.\n55. As the Admin, I want Deactivation to take effect immediately, including for sessions already open, so that there is no window in which a graduated Officer can post.\n56. As the Admin, I want Deactivated Users' Posts and Bylines to remain, so that chapter history is not rewritten when people graduate.\n57. As the Admin, I want to be unable to Deactivate or demote the last active Admin, so that the chapter is never locked out of its own site.\n58. As the Admin handing over, I want to promote my successor before Deactivating myself, so that the handover cannot leave the site without an Admin.\n59. As the Admin, I want the user list to warn me when Pages lose their Assigned editor, so that I reassign them during turnover.\n60. As the Admin, I want to reset another User's password to a temporary one, so that a forgetful Officer can recover without an email server.\n61. As an Editor, I want user management hidden and refused when I try its URLs directly, so that I cannot see or change anyone's account.\n62. As the Admin, I want a setting for the contact line shown to blocked Editors, so that the name and email they are told to contact stay current across turnover.\n\n### Markdown and safety\n\n63. As an Editor, I want basic formatting (headings, bold, italics, lists, links, quotes) to work, so that Posts are readable.\n64. As the Admin, I want all raw HTML in Markdown stripped, so that nobody can embed scripts or markup that is not part of the chapter's design.\n65. As a visitor, I want links that lead off the site to open safely, so that outside pages cannot reach back into the chapter's site.\n66. As a visitor, I want every internal link and file on the public site to use relative paths, so that the site works from the GitHub Pages project URL.\n67. As the Admin, I want all state-changing forms to carry a CSRF token and refuse requests without it, so that another website cannot make my browser change content.\n68. As the Admin, I want Users' emails and login names kept out of the public site, so that members' personal information is never published by the CMS.\n\n### Publishing and Deploy\n\n69. As the Admin, I want `cms publish` to render only Published Posts and Pages into the static site, so that drafts never leave the database.\n70. As the Admin, I want `cms publish` to refuse and explain when any Draft would appear in the output, so that a half-written rush announcement cannot slip through.\n71. As the Admin, I want `cms publish` to show what is new, changed and removed, so that I can review a release before it goes Live.\n72. As the Admin, I want `cms publish` to render Navigation, Home, News and each Post's Byline, so that the generated site is complete and I only run one command.\n73. As the Admin, I want the News page to list Posts newest-first by published date, so that alumni see the latest chapter news first.\n74. As the Admin, I want Home to show the Home Page followed by the 5 latest Posts, so that visitors see current activity straight away.\n75. As the Admin, I want `cms deploy` to ask me to confirm before it pushes, so that I give final approval to everything that becomes Live.\n76. As the Admin, I want `cms deploy` to push only the rendered static site, so that the database, `.env` and secrets are never published.\n77. As the Admin, I want unpublished (set back to Draft) content to disappear from the site at the next release, so that taking something down is possible.\n78. As a visitor (prospective member, alumni, parent or Kenyon staff), I want to read the chapter's news, community service and history without logging in, so that I can learn about the chapter.\n\n### Demo and handover\n\n79. As a grader or a new Admin, I want `scripts/seed_demo.py` to build a demo database with an Admin, an Editor and a mix of Draft and Published content, so that I can use the CMS from a fresh clone with no manual steps.\n80. As the outgoing president, I want a handover checklist in the README, so that my successor knows what to take over (the repository, the database and the image folder) and what to do first.\n\n### Cuttable extras (built last)\n\n81. As the Admin, I want Markdown images from an admin-managed folder to appear in Posts and Pages by relative path, so that the chapter's photos can illustrate its history and service.\n82. As the Admin, I want only images referenced by Published content to be copied into the static site, so that an unapproved photo never goes public.\n83. As an Editor, I want an optional event date on a Post, so that rush and philanthropy events show when they happen.\n84. As a visitor, I want a Post with an event date to show both its published date and \"Event: <date>\", so that I can tell when something was posted from when it happens.\n85. As the Admin, I want `cms backup` to write a dated copy of the database outside the repository, so that one dead laptop does not erase the chapter's content.\n86. As the Admin, I want a username lock for 10 minutes after 5 failed logins, so that password guessing is slow. The lock is keyed on the email.\n87. As the Admin, I want `cms deploy` to warn me and stop if content has changed since the last `cms publish`, so that stale files in the static site are not pushed by accident.\n88. As the Admin, I want the `cms publish` summary to compare against what was last Deployed, so that \"changed\" means changed since the public site was updated.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n**Architecture (fixed by ADR-001 and ADR-002):** a FastAPI admin console with Jinja templates and SQLite runs locally. `cms publish` writes a static site, and `cms deploy` pushes it to the `gh-pages` branch. There is no frontend framework and no build step. This spec adds no dependency. Asking the user is required before adding one.\n\n**Modules**\n- **Users and authentication:** the User record (email, display name, title, Term, role, active flag, password hash, must-change-password flag), argon2 hashing, signed session cookies with an 8-hour lifetime, and a per-request check that rejects Deactivated Users, so old sessions stop working. Login is by email. The wrong-password message is the same whether or not the email exists.\n- **Authorization:** one place that decides \"may this User do this to this item\". Every admin route calls it on the server side. The rules:\n  - Admin may do everything.\n  - An Editor may create Posts, may edit only their own Posts, and may edit only the Pages assigned to them.\n  - Editors may set their own Posts and Assigned Pages to Published, and may set their own Posts back to Draft.\n  - Editors may delete only their own Draft Posts.\n  - Only the Admin may create or delete Pages, assign editors, set Navigation, unlock a Slug, manage Users, or reset passwords.\n  - Everything else read-only for Editors.\n- **CSRF protection:** every state-changing form carries a token, and requests without it are rejected.\n- **Content:** Posts and Pages. A Post has a title, a unique Slug, a Markdown body, status, author, created, updated and published timestamps, and a Byline snapshot (name, title, Term) taken at first Published. A Page has a title, a unique Slug, a Markdown body, status, an Assigned editor, `show_in_nav`, `nav_order`, and an `is_home` flag that is true for exactly one Page. Slugs are generated from the title, lowercase with hyphens, unique within their kind, and locked after first Published except by the Admin. Editing a Published item changes it in place.\n- **Markdown rendering:** a single function that converts Markdown to HTML and then sanitizes it, used by both Preview and the Publish run so they cannot disagree. Raw HTML is stripped. Basic formatting and links are allowed, and outside links get `rel=\"noopener\"`.\n- **Admin console:** dashboard (Pending release first, then Drafts waiting, then my recent items, and for the Admin only Pages needing an editor), content list (status, type and author filters, \"Mine\" shortcut, large status badge, read-only rows for other people's items), editor with Preview (opens in a new tab with a \"draft preview, not public\" banner, refreshed on click), user management, and the blocked-Editor message that names the Admin and the contact line.\n- **Settings:** an Admin-editable contact line shown only inside the console.\n- **Publishing:** reads only Published content, renders pages, Posts, Home, News and Navigation into the static site using relative paths only, then verifies that no Draft appears in the output. Home is the Home Page followed by the 5 latest Posts as title, date and first paragraph. News lists every Post newest-first, with titles and dates, on one page.\n- **CLI:** `cms publish` renders, shows new, changed and removed items, and refuses on any Draft in the output. `cms deploy` is separate, asks for confirmation, then pushes. `cms create-admin <email>` takes a hidden password prompt. `cms reset-password <email>` resets the Admin's own password on the machine. Both take an email, not a username, to match login.\n- **Demo data:** the seed script creates the Admin and Editor from `.env` values (never hard-coded), plus sample Posts and Pages including at least one Draft and one Published item.\n\n**Passwords and sessions:** minimum 12 characters and no other rules. Temporary passwords force a change at next login.\n\n**Cuttable extras (built last, each independent of the core)**\n- **Images:** an admin-managed folder, referenced by relative path in Markdown. The Publish run copies only images referenced by Published content. Without this extra, image syntax is stripped by the sanitizer.\n- **Event date:** an optional field on Posts. A Post with one shows both its published date and \"Event: <date>\". News is still sorted by published date.\n- **`cms backup`:** writes a timestamped copy of the database outside the repository. Never committed.\n- **Login lockout:** keyed on the email, 5 failures locks it for 10 minutes. The message does not reveal whether the email exists.\n- **Deploy fingerprints:** a successful `cms deploy` records a fingerprint of each item, the baseline for \"changed since last Deploy\" in the `cms publish` summary and for the stale-site warning in `cms deploy`. Without this extra, the summary lists every Published item.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n**What makes a good test:** it exercises external behavior only, such as what a User sees or is refused, and what ends up in the generated files. It never reaches into private functions or table layouts. Each acceptance criterion in a ticket should have at least one test that clearly exercises it.\n\n**Two seams, both existing:**\n1. **The HTTP app through the test client** (`client` and the logged-in `client_as(\"admin\" | \"editor\")`). This covers login and logout, roles and permission refusals (including direct URL requests), Posts and Pages (Slug rules, the Draft and Published rules, Assigned editor, Byline snapshot), the dashboard, content list and filters, Preview, user management and Deactivation, and CSRF (replaying each POST with the token removed). Assertions are on status codes, redirects and response HTML.\n2. **Static output and the `cms` commands, against a temporary site folder and a temporary database.** `render_site` covers the content of the output: only Published content, no root-absolute paths, `<script>` and `onerror=` removed, Navigation order, Home and News, bylines with no email or login name. The `cms` command entry point covers `publish` refusing when a Draft would appear and `deploy` asking before pushing, with the actual push stubbed so nothing touches `gh-pages`.\n\n**Prior art:** `tests/conftest.py` already provides `client` and `client_as`, and the seeded users `admin@example.test` and `editor@example.test`. `tests/test_t00.py` shows the style for static output tests (publish into a temp folder, then read the files and check for relative paths). The T00 tests must keep passing.\n\n**Security checklist coverage:** each of the 10 items in the project's security checklist gets at least one test through the seams above, including the editor-cannot-reach-admin-routes and anonymous-is-redirected tests.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Image upload by Editors (stretch goal; for now the Admin adds photos to a folder).\n- Remote access for Editors. The console stays local (ADR-001), and live admin deployment is a stretch goal.\n- Comments, search, or any server-side feature on the public site.\n- Categories, tags and bulk actions in the content list.\n- Revision history and a separate draft copy of a Live item.\n- A public member roster page or any automated listing of members.\n- Email, including emailed password resets.\n- Pagination of News, and live-as-you-type Preview.\n- A \"protected page\" flag. Page permissions come from the Assigned editor.\n- Position-based Page assignment. Pages are assigned to a User.\n- Any change to the stack in the project's dependency list.\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- **Build order:** the 7 required capabilities come first. The five cuttable extras (images, event date, `cms backup`, login lockout, deploy fingerprints) are the last tickets so they can be cut if time runs out. The core must work without them.\n- **Vocabulary:** use the terms in `CONTEXT.md`: Officer, User, Admin, Editor, Deactivated, Term, Byline, Post, Page, Assigned editor, Draft, Published, Live, Publish run, Deploy, Pending release, Navigation and Slug. \"Published\" means ready for release and \"Live\" means actually on the public site as of the latest Deploy.\n- **Personal information:** the CMS controls only what it renders from User records. Whatever an Editor types in a body is the Editor's responsibility, and Preview shows exactly what will be public.\n- **Repo is public:** photos added to the image folder are public the moment they are pushed, so unapproved photos stay out of the folder.\n- **Source material:** the client brief and WordPress field notes in the repository's notes folder, and the grill-with-docs session decisions.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":94,"cache_read_input_tokens":84135,"output_tokens":9349,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":989},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":94,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":9349,"cache_read_input_tokens":84135,"cache_creation_input_tokens":94,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":94},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01YTfCAYRrre6q2edVPzDJp4":{"file_path":"/tmp/claude-1000/-home-faisa-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/6e0298fd-6441-4373-ab13-28afb21c8981/scratchpad/spec.md","content":"## Problem Statement\n\nThe Chi Chapter of Delta Tau Delta at Kenyon College has an outdated website run by one alum who never updates it. Alumni cannot find updates, information is spread out, and active Officers cannot change anything. Prospective members, alumni, parents and Kenyon staff want to learn about the chapter's members, news, community service and history.\n\nThe chapter president needs a site that the Officers themselves can keep current, with these things never happening:\n\n- A graduated Officer can still log in and post.\n- An Editor deletes or changes the chapter history Page, or another Officer's Post.\n- A half-written Draft goes public, such as a rush announcement with the wrong date.\n- Members' personal information ends up public.\n\nThe people running it are college students who are comfortable with computers but not technical, and their roles change hands about once a year.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small CMS in which the president (Admin) and the other Officers (Editors) write Posts and Pages in a local admin console. The Admin runs `cms publish` to render the Published content into a static site, then `cms deploy` to push it to GitHub Pages after confirming. Nothing is Live until the Admin has reviewed and deployed it.\n\nThe console is deliberately plain. It has a dashboard that leads with what is waiting for release, a content list with a large status badge and only the filters that matter, and an editor with a prominent Preview. An Editor can only change their own Posts and the Pages the Admin has assigned to them. Officers who graduate are Deactivated immediately, and their past work and Byline stay.\n\nThe admin console never goes on the public internet (ADR-001). Editors work on a machine that runs the console, such as a shared chapter-house laptop.\n\n### The 7 required capabilities, for this client\n\n1. **Login with hashed passwords.** An Officer logs in with their email and password. Passwords are stored only as argon2 hashes. A wrong password gets a generic refusal that does not reveal whether the email exists. The Admin sets a temporary password for another User, who must change it at next login. The Admin's own recovery is a command on the machine.\n2. **Two roles, Admin and Editor.** The president is the Admin. Every other Officer is an Editor who writes their own Posts and edits only the Pages the Admin assigned to them. Access is enforced in code on every request, not by hiding links.\n3. **Posts.** Title, Slug, Markdown body, Draft or Published, author, and created, updated and published timestamps. Each Post shows a Byline with the author's full name, title and Term, fixed when the Post is first marked Published.\n4. **Pages in public Navigation.** Standing content such as About, History and Community Service has no author and no date. The Admin creates Pages, assigns one Editor to each, and chooses which appear in Navigation and in what order. One Page is the Home page.\n5. **Admin console.** A dashboard, a filterable content list, and an editor with Markdown Preview.\n6. **Admin-only user management with Deactivation.** The Admin creates Users, sets a role, title and Term, resets passwords, and Deactivates Users when they leave office. Deactivated Users are never deleted and cannot log in, even with an old session.\n7. **Static public site via `cms publish`.** `cms publish` renders only Published content into the static site, with sanitized Markdown and relative paths only. It shows what is new, changed or removed, and refuses if any Draft would appear. `cms deploy` is a separate command that confirms with the Admin before pushing to GitHub Pages.\n\n## User Stories\n\n### Login and accounts\n\n1. As the Admin setting up the CMS for the first time, I want `cms create-admin` to ask for my email and a hidden password, so that there is no default password in the code or the demo data.\n10. As an Admin, I want an anonymous visitor to be redirected to login on every admin URL, so that no admin content is ever shown to someone who is not logged in.\n\n### Roles and permissions\n\n11. As an Editor, I want to create Posts and edit only my own, so that I can do my job without being able to damage another Officer's work.\n12. As an Editor, I want to see every Post and Page in the content list but have other people's rows read-only, so that I know what is already written without being able to change it.\n13.
