As an Editor, I want to edit a Published Post in place and have the change reach the site at the next release, so that I can fix a typo without taking the Post down first.\n32. As an Editor, I want Posts that changed since the last Deploy to be marked in the content list, so that I can see which edits are not yet Live.\n\n### Pages and Navigation\n\n33. As the Admin, I want to create a Page and assign it to one Editor, so that every standing area of the site has a named maintainer.\n34. As the Admin, I want to choose which Pages appear in Navigation and their order, so that visitors see About, History and Community Service in a sensible order.\n35. As a visitor, I want the top of every public page to show Home, the chapter's Pages, and News, so that I can find things from anywhere.\n36. As a visitor, I want a Published Page without a Navigation entry to still be reachable by its URL, so that unlisted pages such as a rush information page can be shared directly.\n37. As the Admin, I want one Page flagged as the Home page, so that the site's front door is under my control.\n38. As the Admin, I want only the Admin to be able to delete a Page, so that an Editor cannot remove the chapter history Page.\n39. As the Admin, I want Pages to have no author and no date on the public site, so that standing content reads as the chapter's own voice.\n40. As the Admin, I want Pages whose Assigned editor was Deactivated to be left unassigned and Admin-only, so that nobody inherits access by accident.\n\n### Admin console\n\n41. As an Officer, I want a dashboard that leads with Pending release, so that I see first what is waiting to go public.\n42. As an Officer, I want the dashboard to show Drafts waiting and my own recent items, so that I can pick up where I left off.\n43. As the Admin, I want the dashboard to show Pages needing a new Assigned editor, so that turnover problems are visible.\n44. As an Officer, I want a content list with a large, clearly coloured status badge for Draft and Published, so that I can tell the status at a glance.\n45. As an Officer, I want to filter the content list by status, by type (Post or Page) and by author, so that I can find things quickly.\n46. As an Officer, I want a \"Mine\" shortcut on the content list, so that I can see only my own work in one click.\n47. As an Officer, I want the content list to have no categories, tags or bulk actions, so that it makes sense without a technical background.\n48. As an Editor, I want a Preview button right next to Save, so that I do not have to hunt for it.\n49. As an Editor, I want Preview to render the exact sanitized HTML that the Publish run would write, with the real Byline and Navigation, so that what I check is what visitors will see.\n50. As an Editor, I want Preview to say clearly that it is a draft preview and not public, so that I never confuse it with the live site.\n51. As an Editor, I want to see Markdown I typed with a script or event handler stripped in Preview, so that I find out about unsafe content before it is published.\n\n### User management\n\n52. As the Admin, I want to create a User with an email, display name, title, Term and role, so that a new Officer can start work.\n53. As the Admin, I want to change a User's role, title and Term, so that the console follows who currently holds each position.\n54. As the Admin, I want to Deactivate a User when they leave office, so that a graduated Officer can no longer log in or post.\n55. As the Admin, I want Deactivation to take effect immediately, including for sessions already open, so that there is no window in which a graduated Officer can post.\n56. As the Admin, I want Deactivated Users' Posts and Bylines to remain, so that chapter history is not rewritten when people graduate.\n57. As the Admin, I want to be unable to Deactivate or demote the last active Admin, so that the chapter is never locked out of its own site.\n58. As the Admin handing over, I want to promote my successor before Deactivating myself, so that the handover cannot leave the site without an Admin.\n59. As the Admin, I want the user list to warn me when Pages lose their Assigned editor, so that I reassign them during turnover.\n60. As the Admin, I want to reset another User's password to a temporary one, so that a forgetful Officer can recover without an email server.\n61. As an Editor, I want user management hidden and refused when I try its URLs directly, so that I cannot see or change anyone's account.\n62. As the Admin, I want a setting for the contact line shown to blocked Editors, so that the name and email they are told to contact stay current across turnover.\n\n### Markdown and safety\n\n63. As an Editor, I want basic formatting (headings, bold, italics, lists, links, quotes) to work, so that Posts are readable.\n64. As the Admin, I want all raw HTML in Markdown stripped, so that nobody can embed scripts or markup that is not part of the chapter's design.\n65. As a visitor, I want links that lead off the site to open safely, so that outside pages cannot reach back into the chapter's site.\n66. As a visitor, I want every internal link and file on the public site to use relative paths, so that the site works from the GitHub Pages project URL.\n67. As the Admin, I want all state-changing forms to carry a CSRF token and refuse requests without it, so that another website cannot make my browser change content.\n68. As the Admin, I want Users' emails and login names kept out of the public site, so that members' personal information is never published by the CMS.\n\n### Publishing and Deploy\n\n69. As the Admin, I want `cms publish` to render only Published Posts and Pages into the static site, so that drafts never leave the database.\n70. As the Admin, I want `cms publish` to refuse and explain when any Draft would appear in the output, so that a half-written rush announcement cannot slip through.\n71. As the Admin, I want `cms publish` to show what is new, changed and removed, so that I can review a release before it goes Live.\n72. As the Admin, I want `cms publish` to render Navigation, Home, News and each Post's Byline, so that the generated site is complete and I only run one command.\n73. As the Admin, I want the News page to list Posts newest-first by published date, so that alumni see the latest chapter news first.\n74. As the Admin, I want Home to show the Home Page followed by the 5 latest Posts, so that visitors see current activity straight away.\n75. As the Admin, I want `cms deploy` to ask me to confirm before it pushes, so that I give final approval to everything that becomes Live.\n76. As the Admin, I want `cms deploy` to push only the rendered static site, so that the database, `.env` and secrets are never published.\n77. As the Admin, I want unpublished (set back to Draft) content to disappear from the site at the next release, so that taking something down is possible.\n78. As a visitor (prospective member, alumni, parent or Kenyon staff), I want to read the chapter's news, community service and history without logging in, so that I can learn about the chapter.\n\n### Demo and handover\n\n79. As a grader or a new Admin, I want `scripts/seed_demo.py` to build a demo database with an Admin, an Editor and a mix of Draft and Published content, so that I can use the CMS from a fresh clone with no manual steps.\n80. As the outgoing president, I want a handover checklist in the README, so that my successor knows what to take over (the repository, the database and the image folder) and what to do first.\n\n### Cuttable extras (built last)\n\n81. As the Admin, I want Markdown images from an admin-managed folder to appear in Posts and Pages by relative path, so that the chapter's photos can illustrate its history and service.\n82. As the Admin, I want only images referenced by Published content to be copied into the static site, so that an unapproved photo never goes public.\n83. As an Editor, I want an optional event date on a Post, so that rush and philanthropy events show when they happen.\n84. As a visitor, I want a Post with an event date to show both its published date and \"Event: <date>\", so that I can tell when something was posted from when it happens.\n85. As the Admin, I want `cms backup` to write a dated copy of the database outside the repository, so that one dead laptop does not erase the chapter's content.\n86. As the Admin, I want a username lock for 10 minutes after 5 failed logins, so that password guessing is slow. The lock is keyed on the email.\n87. As the Admin, I want `cms deploy` to warn me and stop if content has changed since the last `cms publish`, so that stale files in the static site are not pushed by accident.\n88. As the Admin, I want the `cms publish` summary to compare against what was last Deployed, so that \"changed\" means changed since the public site was updated.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n**Architecture (fixed by ADR-001 and ADR-002):** a FastAPI admin console with Jinja templates and SQLite runs locally. `cms publish` writes a static site, and `cms deploy` pushes it to the `gh-pages` branch. There is no frontend framework and no build step. This spec adds no dependency. Asking the user is required before adding one.\n\n**Modules**\n- **Users and authentication:** the User record (email, display name, title, Term, role, active flag, password hash, must-change-password flag), argon2 hashing, signed session cookies with an 8-hour lifetime, and a per-request check that rejects Deactivated Users, so old sessions stop working. Login is by email. The wrong-password message is the same whether or not the email exists.\n- **Authorization:** one place that decides \"may this User do this to this item\". Every admin route calls it on the server side. The rules:\n  - Admin may do everything.\n  - An Editor may create Posts, may edit only their own Posts, and may edit only the Pages assigned to them.\n  - Editors may set their own Posts and Assigned Pages to Published, and may set their own Posts back to Draft.\n  - Editors may delete only their own Draft Posts.\n  - Only the Admin may create or delete Pages, assign editors, set Navigation, unlock a Slug, manage Users, or reset passwords.\n  - Everything else read-only for Editors.\n- **CSRF protection:** every state-changing form carries a token, and requests without it are rejected.\n- **Content:** Posts and Pages. A Post has a title, a unique Slug, a Markdown body, status, author, created, updated and published timestamps, and a Byline snapshot (name, title, Term) taken at first Published. A Page has a title, a unique Slug, a Markdown body, status, an Assigned editor, `show_in_nav`, `nav_order`, and an `is_home` flag that is true for exactly one Page. Slugs are generated from the title, lowercase with hyphens, unique within their kind, and locked after first Published except by the Admin. Editing a Published item changes it in place.\n- **Markdown rendering:** a single function that converts Markdown to HTML and then sanitizes it, used by both Preview and the Publish run so they cannot disagree. Raw HTML is stripped. Basic formatting and links are allowed, and outside links get `rel=\"noopener\"`.\n- **Admin console:** dashboard (Pending release first, then Drafts waiting, then my recent items, and for the Admin only Pages needing an editor), content list (status, type and author filters, \"Mine\" shortcut, large status badge, read-only rows for other people's items), editor with Preview (opens in a new tab with a \"draft preview, not public\" banner, refreshed on click), user management, and the blocked-Editor message that names the Admin and the contact line.\n- **Settings:** an Admin-editable contact line shown only inside the console.\n- **Publishing:** reads only Published content, renders pages, Posts, Home, News and Navigation into the static site using relative paths only, then verifies that no Draft appears in the output. Home is the Home Page followed by the 5 latest Posts as title, date and first paragraph. News lists every Post newest-first, with titles and dates, on one page.\n- **CLI:** `cms publish` renders, shows new, changed and removed items, and refuses on any Draft in the output. `cms deploy` is separate, asks for confirmation, then pushes. `cms create-admin <email>` takes a hidden password prompt. `cms reset-password <email>` resets the Admin's own password on the machine. Both take an email, not a username, to match login.\n- **Demo data:** the seed script creates the Admin and Editor from `.env` values (never hard-coded), plus sample Posts and Pages including at least one Draft and one Published item.\n\n**Passwords and sessions:** minimum 12 characters and no other rules. Temporary passwords force a change at next login.\n\n**Cuttable extras (built last, each independent of the core)**\n- **Images:** an admin-managed folder, referenced by relative path in Markdown. The Publish run copies only images referenced by Published content. Without this extra, image syntax is stripped by the sanitizer.\n- **Event date:** an optional field on Posts. A Post with one shows both its published date and \"Event: <date>\". News is still sorted by published date.\n- **`cms backup`:** writes a timestamped copy of the database outside the repository. Never committed.\n- **Login lockout:** keyed on the email, 5 failures locks it for 10 minutes. The message does not reveal whether the email exists.\n- **Deploy fingerprints:** a successful `cms deploy` records a fingerprint of each item, the baseline for \"changed since last Deploy\" in the `cms publish` summary and for the stale-site warning in `cms deploy`. Without this extra, the summary lists every Published item.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n**What makes a good test:** it exercises external behavior only, such as what a User sees or is refused, and what ends up in the generated files. It never reaches into private functions or table layouts. Each acceptance criterion in a ticket should have at least one test that clearly exercises it.\n\n**Two seams, both existing:**\n1. **The HTTP app through the test client** (`client` and the logged-in `client_as(\"admin\" | \"editor\")`). This covers login and logout, roles and permission refusals (including direct URL requests), Posts and Pages (Slug rules, the Draft and Published rules, Assigned editor, Byline snapshot), the dashboard, content list and filters, Preview, user management and Deactivation, and CSRF (replaying each POST with the token removed). Assertions are on status codes, redirects and response HTML.\n2. **Static output and the `cms` commands, against a temporary site folder and a temporary database.** `render_site` covers the content of the output: only Published content, no root-absolute paths, `<script>` and `onerror=` removed, Navigation order, Home and News, bylines with no email or login name. The `cms` command entry point covers `publish` refusing when a Draft would appear and `deploy` asking before pushing, with the actual push stubbed so nothing touches `gh-pages`.\n\n**Prior art:** `tests/conftest.py` already provides `client` and `client_as`, and the seeded users `admin@example.test` and `editor@example.test`. `tests/test_t00.py` shows the style for static output tests (publish into a temp folder, then read the files and check for relative paths). The T00 tests must keep passing.\n\n**Security checklist coverage:** each of the 10 items in the project's security checklist gets at least one test through the seams above, including the editor-cannot-reach-admin-routes and anonymous-is-redirected tests.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Image upload by Editors (stretch goal; for now the Admin adds photos to a folder).\n- Remote access for Editors. The console stays local (ADR-001), and live admin deployment is a stretch goal.\n- Comments, search, or any server-side feature on the public site.\n- Categories, tags and bulk actions in the content list.\n- Revision history and a separate draft copy of a Live item.\n- A public member roster page or any automated listing of members.\n- Email, including emailed password resets.\n- Pagination of News, and live-as-you-type Preview.\n- A \"protected page\" flag. Page permissions come from the Assigned editor.\n- Position-based Page assignment. Pages are assigned to a User.\n- Any change to the stack in the project's dependency list.\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- **Build order:** the 7 required capabilities come first. The five cuttable extras (images, event date, `cms backup`, login lockout, deploy fingerprints) are the last tickets so they can be cut if time runs out. The core must work without them.\n- **Vocabulary:** use the terms in `CONTEXT.md`: Officer, User, Admin, Editor, Deactivated, Term, Byline, Post, Page, Assigned editor, Draft, Published, Live, Publish run, Deploy, Pending release, Navigation and Slug. \"Published\" means ready for release and \"Live\" means actually on the public site as of the latest Deploy.\n- **Personal information:** the CMS controls only what it renders from User records. {"parentUuid":"7c28d465-99d5-43e1-89a4-04c8a29d8864","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"ac245842-8c89-497e-96db-025c379edccf","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01YTfCAYRrre6q2edVPzDJp4","type":"tool_result","content":"File created successfully at: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-faisa-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/6e0298fd-6441-4373-ab13-28afb21c8981/scratchpad/spec.md (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"ff1c16bc-0fa5-4579-a469-fe5009e215cb","timestamp":"2026-10-06T21:39:23.248Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"create","filePath":"/tmp/claude-1000/-home-faisa-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/6e0298fd-6441-4373-ab13-28afb21c8981/scratchpad/spec.md","content":"## Problem Statement\n\nThe Chi Chapter of Delta Tau Delta at Kenyon College has an outdated website run by one alum who never updates it. Alumni cannot find updates, information is spread out, and active Officers cannot change anything. Prospective members, alumni, parents and Kenyon staff want to learn about the chapter's members, news, community service and history.\n\nThe chapter president needs a site that the Officers themselves can keep current, with these things never happening:\n\n- A graduated Officer can still log in and post.\n- An Editor deletes or changes the chapter history Page, or another Officer's Post.\n- A half-written Draft goes public, such as a rush announcement with the wrong date.\n- Members' personal information ends up public.\n\nThe people running it are college students who are comfortable with computers but not technical, and their roles change hands about once a year.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small CMS in which the president (Admin) and the other Officers (Editors) write Posts and Pages in a local admin console. The Admin runs `cms publish` to render the Published content into a static site, then `cms deploy` to push it to GitHub Pages after confirming. Nothing is Live until the Admin has reviewed and deployed it.\n\nThe console is deliberately plain. It has a dashboard that leads with what is waiting for release, a content list with a large status badge and only the filters that matter, and an editor with a prominent Preview. An Editor can only change their own Posts and the Pages the Admin has assigned to them. Officers who graduate are Deactivated immediately, and their past work and Byline stay.\n\nThe admin console never goes on the public internet (ADR-001). Editors work on a machine that runs the console, such as a shared chapter-house laptop.\n\n### The 7 required capabilities, for this client\n\n1. **Login with hashed passwords.** An Officer logs in with their email and password. Passwords are stored only as argon2 hashes. A wrong password gets a generic refusal that does not reveal whether the email exists. The Admin sets a temporary password for another User, who must change it at next login. The Admin's own recovery is a command on the machine.\n2. **Two roles, Admin and Editor.** The president is the Admin. Every other Officer is an Editor who writes their own Posts and edits only the Pages the Admin assigned to them. Access is enforced in code on every request, not by hiding links.\n3. **Posts.** Title, Slug, Markdown body, Draft or Published, author, and created, updated and published timestamps. Each Post shows a Byline with the author's full name, title and Term, fixed when the Post is first marked Published.\n4. **Pages in public Navigation.** Standing content such as About, History and Community Service has no author and no date. The Admin creates Pages, assigns one Editor to each, and chooses which appear in Navigation and in what order. One Page is the Home page.\n5. **Admin console.** A dashboard, a filterable content list, and an editor with Markdown Preview.\n6. **Admin-only user management with Deactivation.** The Admin creates Users, sets a role, title and Term, resets passwords, and Deactivates Users when they leave office. Deactivated Users are never deleted and cannot log in, even with an old session.\n7. **Static public site via `cms publish`.** `cms publish` renders only Published content into the static site, with sanitized Markdown and relative paths only. It shows what is new, changed or removed, and refuses if any Draft would appear. `cms deploy` is a separate command that confirms with the Admin before pushing to GitHub Pages.\n\n## User Stories\n\n### Login and accounts\n\n1. As an Officer, I want to log in with my email and password, so that I can reach the console without a separate username.\n2. As an Officer, I want to log out, so that the next person on a shared chapter laptop cannot use my account.\n3. As an Officer who typed a wrong password, I want a clear refusal that does not say whether my email exists, so that nobody can use the login form to find out who has an account.\n4. As an Officer who was just given a temporary password, I want to be made to choose my own at first login, so that the Admin never knows my real password.\n5. As an Officer choosing a password, I want to be told the minimum length, so that I do not guess at hidden rules.\n6. As the Admin, I want a session to end after 8 hours, so that a logged-in shared laptop does not stay open overnight.\n7. As the Admin, I want passwords stored only as argon2 hashes and never logged, so that a copied database does not expose anyone's password.\n8. As the Admin who forgot my own password, I want a command on the machine to reset it, so that I am not locked out when no email server exists.\n9. As the Admin setting up the CMS for the first time, I want `cms create-admin` to ask for my email and a hidden password, so that there is no default password in the code or the demo data.\n10. As an Admin, I want an anonymous visitor to be redirected to login on every admin URL, so that no admin content is ever shown to someone who is not logged in.\n\n### Roles and permissions\n\n11. As an Editor, I want to create Posts and edit only my own, so that I can do my job without being able to damage another Officer's work.\n12. As an Editor, I want to see every Post and Page in the content list but have other people's rows read-only, so that I know what is already written without being able to change it.\n13. As an Editor, I want to edit a Page the Admin assigned to me, so that I can keep my area (for example Community Service or History) current without needing the president.\n14. As an Editor, I want other Editors to be unable to edit my Assigned Page, so that my work is not overwritten by someone else.\n15. As an Editor, I want to mark my own Posts and my Assigned Pages Published, so that I am not waiting on the president for every step.\n16. As an Editor, I want to set my own Post back to Draft, so that I can take something down that I got wrong.\n17. As an Editor, I want to delete my own Drafts, so that I can clean up abandoned writing.\n18. As an Editor who tries to reach a page I am not allowed to use, I want a short message naming the current Admin and how to reach them, so that I know who to ask for higher permission.\n19. As an Editor, I want controls I cannot use to be hidden, so that the console is not cluttered with buttons that do nothing.\n20. As the Admin, I want an Editor who requests an admin-only URL directly to be refused (403 or redirect), so that hiding links is never the only protection.\n21. As the Admin, I want to edit and delete any Post or Page, so that I can correct problems when an Officer is unavailable.\n22. As the Admin, I want a deleted-Post rule that lets Editors delete only Drafts, so that a published announcement cannot be erased in one click.\n\n### Posts\n\n23. As an Editor, I want to write a Post with a title and a Markdown body, so that I can post news without knowing HTML.\n24. As the Admin, I want a setting for the contact line shown to blocked Editors, so that the name and email they are told to contact stay current across turnover.\n\n### Markdown and safety\n\n63. As an Editor, I want basic formatting (headings, bold, italics, lists, links, quotes) to work, so that Posts are readable.\n64. As the Admin, I want all raw HTML in Markdown stripped, so that nobody can embed scripts or markup that is not part of the chapter's design.\n65. As a visitor, I want links that lead off the site to open safely, so that outside pages cannot reach back into the chapter's site.\n66. As a visitor, I want every internal link and file on the public site to use relative paths, so that the site works from the GitHub Pages project URL.\n67. As the Admin, I want all state-changing forms to carry a CSRF token and refuse requests without it, so that another website cannot make my browser change content.\n68. As the Admin, I want Users' emails and login names kept out of the public site, so that members' personal information is never published by the CMS.\n\n### Publishing and Deploy\n\n69. As the Admin, I want `cms publish` to render only Published Posts and Pages into the static site, so that drafts never leave the database.\n70. As the Admin, I want `cms publish` to refuse and explain when any Draft would appear in the output, so that a half-written rush announcement cannot slip through.\n71. As the Admin, I want `cms publish` to show what is new, changed and removed, so that I can review a release before it goes Live.\n72. As the Admin, I want `cms publish` to render Navigation, Home, News and each Post's Byline, so that the generated site is complete and I only run one command.\n73. As the Admin, I want the News page to list Posts newest-first by published date, so that alumni see the latest chapter news first.\n74. As the Admin, I want Home to show the Home Page followed by the 5 latest Posts, so that visitors see current activity straight away.\n75. As the Admin, I want `cms deploy` to ask me to confirm before it pushes, so that I give final approval to everything that becomes Live.\n76. As the Admin, I want `cms deploy` to push only the rendered static site, so that the database, `.env` and secrets are never published.\n77. As the Admin, I want unpublished (set back to Draft) content to disappear from the site at the next release, so that taking something down is possible.\n78. As a visitor (prospective member, alumni, parent or Kenyon staff), I want to read the chapter's news, community service and history without logging in, so that I can learn about the chapter.\n\n### Demo and handover\n\n79. As a grader or a new Admin, I want `scripts/seed_demo.py` to build a demo database with an Admin, an Editor and a mix of Draft and Published content, so that I can use the CMS from a fresh clone with no manual steps.\n80. As the outgoing president, I want a handover checklist in the README, so that my successor knows what to take over (the repository, the database and the image folder) and what to do first.\n\n### Cuttable extras (built last)\n\n81. As the Admin, I want Markdown images from an admin-managed folder to appear in Posts and Pages by relative path, so that the chapter's photos can illustrate its history and service.\n82. As the Admin, I want only images referenced by Published content to be copied into the static site, so that an unapproved photo never goes public.\n83. As an Editor, I want an optional event date on a Post, so that rush and philanthropy events show when they happen.\n84. As a visitor, I want a Post with an event date to show both its published date and \"Event: <date>\", so that I can tell when something was posted from when it happens.\n85. As the Admin, I want `cms backup` to write a dated copy of the database outside the repository, so that one dead laptop does not erase the chapter's content.\n86. As the Admin, I want a username lock for 10 minutes after 5 failed logins, so that password guessing is slow. The lock is keyed on the email.\n87. As the Admin, I want `cms deploy` to warn me and stop if content has changed since the last `cms publish`, so that stale files in the static site are not pushed by accident.\n88. As the Admin, I want the `cms publish` summary to compare against what was last Deployed, so that \"changed\" means changed since the public site was updated.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n**Architecture (fixed by ADR-001 and ADR-002):** a FastAPI admin console with Jinja templates and SQLite runs locally. `cms publish` writes a static site, and `cms deploy` pushes it to the `gh-pages` branch. There is no frontend framework and no build step. This spec adds no dependency. Asking the user is required before adding one.\n\n**Modules**\n- **Users and authentication:** the User record (email, display name, title, Term, role, active flag, password hash, must-change-password flag), argon2 hashing, signed session cookies with an 8-hour lifetime, and a per-request check that rejects Deactivated Users, so old sessions stop working. Login is by email. The wrong-password message is the same whether or not the email exists.\n- **Authorization:** one place that decides \"may this User do this to this item\". Every admin route calls it on the server side. The rules:\n  - Admin may do everything.\n  - An Editor may create Posts, may edit only their own Posts, and may edit only the Pages assigned to them.\n  - Editors may set their own Posts and Assigned Pages to Published, and may set their own Posts back to Draft.\n  - Editors may delete only their own Draft Posts.\n  - Only the Admin may create or delete Pages, assign editors, set Navigation, unlock a Slug, manage Users, or reset passwords.\n  - Everything else read-only for Editors.\n- **CSRF protection:** every state-changing form carries a token, and requests without it are rejected.\n- **Content:** Posts and Pages. A Post has a title, a unique Slug, a Markdown body, status, author, created, updated and published timestamps, and a Byline snapshot (name, title, Term) taken at first Published. A Page has a title, a unique Slug, a Markdown body, status, an Assigned editor, `show_in_nav`, `nav_order`, and an `is_home` flag that is true for exactly one Page. Slugs are generated from the title, lowercase with hyphens, unique within their kind, and locked after first Published except by the Admin. Editing a Published item changes it in place.\n- **Markdown rendering:** a single function that converts Markdown to HTML and then sanitizes it, used by both Preview and the Publish run so they cannot disagree. Raw HTML is stripped. Basic formatting and links are allowed, and outside links get `rel=\"noopener\"`.\n- **Admin console:** dashboard (Pending release first, then Drafts waiting, then my recent items, and for the Admin only Pages needing an editor), content list (status, type and author filters, \"Mine\" shortcut, large status badge, read-only rows for other people's items), editor with Preview (opens in a new tab with a \"draft preview, not public\" banner, refreshed on click), user management, and the blocked-Editor message that names the Admin and the contact line.\n- **Settings:** an Admin-editable contact line shown only inside the console.\n- **Publishing:** reads only Published content, renders pages, Posts, Home, News and Navigation into the static site using relative paths only, then verifies that no Draft appears in the output. Home is the Home Page followed by the 5 latest Posts as title, date and first paragraph. News lists every Post newest-first, with titles and dates, on one page.\n- **CLI:** `cms publish` renders, shows new, changed and removed items, and refuses on any Draft in the output. `cms deploy` is separate, asks for confirmation, then pushes. `cms create-admin <email>` takes a hidden password prompt. `cms reset-password <email>` resets the Admin's own password on the machine. Both take an email, not a username, to match login.\n- **Demo data:** the seed script creates the Admin and Editor from `.env` values (never hard-coded), plus sample Posts and Pages including at least one Draft and one Published item.\n\n**Passwords and sessions:** minimum 12 characters and no other rules. Temporary passwords force a change at next login.\n\n**Cuttable extras (built last, each independent of the core)**\n- **Images:** an admin-managed folder, referenced by relative path in Markdown. The Publish run copies only images referenced by Published content. Without this extra, image syntax is stripped by the sanitizer.\n- **Event date:** an optional field on Posts. A Post with one shows both its published date and \"Event: <date>\". News is still sorted by published date.\n- **`cms backup`:** writes a timestamped copy of the database outside the repository. Never committed.\n- **Login lockout:** keyed on the email, 5 failures locks it for 10 minutes. The message does not reveal whether the email exists.\n- **Deploy fingerprints:** a successful `cms deploy` records a fingerprint of each item, the baseline for \"changed since last Deploy\" in the `cms publish` summary and for the stale-site warning in `cms deploy`. Without this extra, the summary lists every Published item.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n**What makes a good test:** it exercises external behavior only, such as what a User sees or is refused, and what ends up in the generated files. It never reaches into private functions or table layouts. Each acceptance criterion in a ticket should have at least one test that clearly exercises it.\n\n**Two seams, both existing:**\n1. **The HTTP app through the test client** (`client` and the logged-in `client_as(\"admin\" | \"editor\")`). This covers login and logout, roles and permission refusals (including direct URL requests), Posts and Pages (Slug rules, the Draft and Published rules, Assigned editor, Byline snapshot), the dashboard, content list and filters, Preview, user management and Deactivation, and CSRF (replaying each POST with the token removed). Assertions are on status codes, redirects and response HTML.\n2. **Static output and the `cms` commands, against a temporary site folder and a temporary database.** `render_site` covers the content of the output: only Published content, no root-absolute paths, `<script>` and `onerror=` removed, Navigation order, Home and News, bylines with no email or login name. The `cms` command entry point covers `publish` refusing when a Draft would appear and `deploy` asking before pushing, with the actual push stubbed so nothing touches `gh-pages`.\n\n**Prior art:** `tests/conftest.py` already provides `client` and `client_as`, and the seeded users `admin@example.test` and `editor@example.test`. `tests/test_t00.py` shows the style for static output tests (publish into a temp folder, then read the files and check for relative paths). The T00 tests must keep passing.\n\n**Security checklist coverage:** each of the 10 items in the project's security checklist gets at least one test through the seams above, including the editor-cannot-reach-admin-routes and anonymous-is-redirected tests.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Image upload by Editors (stretch goal; for now the Admin adds photos to a folder).\n- Remote access for Editors. The console stays local (ADR-001), and live admin deployment is a stretch goal.\n- Comments, search, or any server-side feature on the public site.\n- Categories, tags and bulk actions in the content list.\n- Revision history and a separate draft copy of a Live item.\n- A public member roster page or any automated listing of members.\n- Email, including emailed password resets.\n- Pagination of News, and live-as-you-type Preview.\n- A \"protected page\" flag. Page permissions come from the Assigned editor.\n- Position-based Page assignment. Pages are assigned to a User.\n- Any change to the stack in the project's dependency list.\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- **Build order:** the 7 required capabilities come first. The five cuttable extras (images, event date, `cms backup`, login lockout, deploy fingerprints) are the last tickets so they can be cut if time runs out. The core must work without them.\n- **Vocabulary:** use the terms in `CONTEXT.md`: Officer, User, Admin, Editor, Deactivated, Term, Byline, Post, Page, Assigned editor, Draft, Published, Live, Publish run, Deploy, Pending release, Navigation and Slug. \"Published\" means ready for release and \"Live\" means actually on the public site as of the latest Deploy.\n- **Personal information:** the CMS controls only what it renders from User records. Whatever an Editor types in a body is the Editor's responsibility, and Preview shows exactly what will be public.\n- **Repo is public:** photos added to the image folder are public the moment they are pushed, so unapproved photos stay out of the folder.\n- **Source material:** the client brief and WordPress field notes in the repository's notes folder, and the grill-with-docs session decisions.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"7c28d465-99d5-43e1-89a4-04c8a29d8864","session_id":"4b1a37e3-ea11-48e9-baa9-b66b752b7a0d","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/faisa/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"6e0298fd-6441-4373-ab13-28afb21c8981","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"619c7174-7673-4721-9752-20ca07ed8d42","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"bdcb5021-4389-47b7-aae7-5ad3d6b115ed","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /home/faisa/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/.claude/skills/to-tickets\n\n# To Tickets\n\nBreak a plan, spec, or conversation into a set of **tickets**: tracer-bullet vertical slices, each declaring the tickets that **block** it.\n\nThe issue tracker and triage label vocabulary should have been provided to you. If not, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Gather context\n\nWork from whatever is already in the conversation context. If the user passes a reference (a spec path, an issue number or URL) as an argument, fetch it and read its full body and comments.\n\n### 2. Explore the codebase (optional)\n\nIf you have not already explored the codebase, do so to understand the current state of the code. Ticket titles and descriptions should use the project's domain glossary vocabulary, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.\n\nLook for opportunities to prefactor the code to make the implementation easier. \"Make the change easy, then make the easy change.\"\n\n### 3. Draft vertical slices\n\nBreak the work into **tracer bullet** tickets.\n\n<vertical-slice-rules>\n\n- Each slice cuts a narrow but COMPLETE path through every layer (schema, API, UI, tests): vertical, NOT a horizontal slice of one layer\n- A completed slice is demoable or verifiable on its own\n- Each slice is sized to fit in a single fresh context window\n- Any prefactoring should be done first\n\n</vertical-slice-rules>\n\nGive each ticket its **blocking edges**: the other tickets that must complete before it can start. A ticket with no blockers can start immediately.\n\n**Wide refactors are the exception to vertical slicing.** A **wide refactor** is one mechanical change (rename a column, retype a shared symbol) whose **blast radius** fans across the whole codebase, so a single edit breaks thousands of call sites at once and no vertical slice can land green. Don't force it into a tracer bullet; sequence it as **expand–contract**. First expand: add the new form beside the old so nothing breaks. Then migrate the call sites over in batches sized by blast radius (per package, per directory), each batch its own ticket blocked by the expand, keeping CI green batch to batch because the old form still exists. Finally contract: delete the old form once no caller remains, in a ticket blocked by every migrate batch. When even the batches can't stay green alone, keep the sequence but let them share an integration branch that all block a final integrate-and-verify ticket; green is promised only there.\n\n### 4. Quiz the user\n\nPresent the proposed breakdown as a numbered list. For each ticket, show:\n\n- **Title**: short descriptive name\n- **Blocked by**: which other tickets (if any) must complete first\n- **What it delivers**: the end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work\n\nAsk the user:\n\n- Does the granularity feel right? (too coarse / too fine)\n- Are the blocking edges correct: does each ticket only depend on tickets that genuinely gate it?\n- Should any tickets be merged or split further?\n\nIterate until the user approves the breakdown.\n\n### 5. Publish the tickets to the configured tracker\n\nPublish the approved tickets. **How** depends on the tracker `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` configured; the tickets are the same either way, only the shape of the blocking edges changes:\n\n- **Local files** → write one file per ticket under `.scratch/<feature-slug>/issues/<NN>-<slug>.md`, numbered from `01` in dependency order (blockers first). Each file's \"Blocked by\" lists the numbers/titles it depends on. Use the per-ticket file template below: one ticket per file, never a single combined file.\n- **A real issue tracker (GitHub, Linear, …)** → publish one issue per ticket in dependency order (blockers first) so each ticket's blocking edges can reference real identifiers. Use the platform's native blocking relationship where it has one; otherwise set each ticket's \"Blocked by\" to the blocking issues. If the source was an existing issue, make each ticket its sub-issue (tracker doc's operation). Apply the `ready-for-agent` triage label unless instructed otherwise; the tickets are agent-grabbable by construction.\n\nWork the **frontier**: any ticket whose blockers are all done. For a purely linear chain that means top to bottom.\n\nDo NOT close or modify any parent issue.\n\n<local-ticket-template>\n\n# <NN>: <Ticket title>\n\n**What to build:** the end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work, from the user's perspective, not a layer-by-layer implementation list.\n\n**Blocked by:** the numbers/titles of the tickets that gate this one, or \"None (can start immediately)\".\n\n**Status:** ready-for-agent\n\n- [ ] Acceptance criterion 1\n- [ ] Acceptance criterion 2\n\n</local-ticket-template>\n\n<issue-template>\n\n## Parent\n\nA reference to the parent issue on the tracker (if the source was an existing issue, otherwise omit this section).\n\n## What to build\n\nThe end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work, from the user's perspective, not layer-by-layer implementation.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] Criterion 1\n- [ ] Criterion 2\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- A reference to each blocking ticket, or \"None (can start immediately)\". Omit this section when blockers were set as native edges.\n\n</issue-template>\n\nIn either form, avoid specific file paths or code snippets: they go stale fast. Exception: if a prototype produced a snippet that encodes a decision more precisely than prose can (state machine, reducer, schema, type shape), inline it and note briefly that it came from a prototype. Trim to the decision-rich parts, not a working demo, just the important bits.\n"}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"ec7bdf48-295e-42e3-b5ba-5361717864ef","timestamp":"2026-10-06T21:42:36.389Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/faisa/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"6e0298fd-6441-4373-ab13-28afb21c8981","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"7aadd442-38e3-4144-9b79-f5e47759f521","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011CfmiJTqLL9b7BiziZWEgq","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I've set the phase to `tickets` and re-read spec #1. I haven't published anything yet. Below is the proposed breakdown, with 8 core tickets and 5 cuttable stretch tickets, for you to approve.\n\nI numbered the tickets so the early ones give you something demoable and Live as soon as possible. A visitor can read a Published Post on GitHub Pages after T04. Nothing starts until the ticket before it is done, and each ticket fits in one fresh session.\n\n## Core tickets (label `ticket`)\n\n| # | Title | Blocked by | What it delivers |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| **T01** | Login, logout and CSRF | None | An Officer logs in with email and password (argon2, 8-hour session, generic refusal). Logout works, anonymous visitors are redirected, and every POST needs a CSRF token. The seed script creates the Admin and Editor from `.env`, and `cms create-admin <email>` works. |\n| **T02** | Posts with editor and Preview | T01 | An Editor writes a Post (title, auto-Slug, Markdown), saves a Draft, marks it Published, or sets it back to Draft. Editors can edit only their own Posts, and delete only their own Drafts. The Slug is locked after first Published, and the Byline snapshot is taken then. Preview uses the shared sanitized renderer and shows the \"not public\" banner. |\n| **T03** | `cms publish`: Posts to a static site | T02 | `cms publish` renders Home (latest 5 Posts), News and each Post into the static site. It uses relative paths only and sanitized HTML, and omits emails and login names. It lists what it is rendering and refuses if any Draft would appear. |\n| **T04** | `cms deploy`, and the site live on Pages | T03 | `cms deploy` is its own command. It asks for confirmation, then pushes `site/` to `gh-pages`, and records when it last ran. A Published Post is Live on GitHub Pages. The README gets the handover checklist. |\n| **T05** | User management, roles and Deactivation | T01 | The Admin creates Users with a role, title and Term, edits them, and Deactivates them. Deactivation cuts open sessions immediately, and the last active Admin can't be Deactivated or demoted. Editors are refused at every admin-only URL. A blocked Editor sees the Admin's name and contact line, which the Admin can set. |\n| **T06** | Temporary passwords and recovery | T05 | The Admin resets a User's password to a temporary one, and that User must change it at next login (12-character minimum). `cms reset-password <email>` works on the machine. |\n| **T07** | Pages, Assigned editor and Navigation | T03, T05 | The Admin creates Pages, assigns one Editor, and sets Navigation order and show/hide. One Page is flagged Home. The Assigned editor and the Admin can edit it, and other Editors are refused. Only the Admin can delete. A Deactivated editor's Pages become unassigned with a warning. `cms publish` renders Pages and Navigation. |\n| **T08** | Dashboard and content list | T02, T04, T07 | The dashboard shows Pending release first, then Drafts waiting, then my recent items, plus Pages needing an editor for the Admin. The content list has status, type and author filters, a \"Mine\" shortcut, and a large status badge. Other people's rows are read-only. |\n\n## Stretch tickets (label `stretch`, built last, each cuttable)\n\n| # | Title | Blocked by | What it delivers |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| **T09** | Images from the admin folder | T03 | Markdown images by relative path appear in Preview and the static site. Only images referenced by Published content are copied. |\n| **T10** | Optional event date on Posts | T02, T03 | An Editor can set an event date, and a Post shows \"Event: <date>\" beside its published date. |\n| **T11** | `cms backup` | T01 | Writes a dated copy of the database outside the repo. |\n| **T12** | Login lockout | T01 | 5 failed logins lock that email for 10 minutes, with a generic message. |\n| **T13** | Deploy fingerprints | T04, T03 | `cms deploy` records a fingerprint per item. The `cms publish` summary then lists only new, changed and removed items. `cms deploy` warns and stops if content changed since the last `cms publish`. |\n\n## Questions for you\n\n1. **Granularity:** T02 (Posts plus Preview plus Slug rules plus Byline) is the biggest, and T07 is next. Should either be split, or is each a fair single session?\n2. **Blocking edges:** I made T05 depend only on T01, so the Admin tickets don't wait on Posts. Is that the right call, or do you want T05 later?\n3. **Merges:** should T06 (password reset) merge into T05, making 7 core tickets? Or stay separate so each stays small? The rubric wants 7–9 core, so both fit.\n4. **A decision to confirm: Pending release without fingerprints.** The core dashboard needs to know what has changed since the last Deploy. As planned, T04 records a last-deployed time and the dashboard counts Published items updated after it, or all Published items if it was never deployed. T13 later makes this exact. It costs a few false \"pending\" items until T13, which I think is fine for a cuttable extra.\n\nTell me what to change, or say \"approved\", and I'll publish the 13 issues in dependency order. Each gets acceptance criteria and a \"Blocked by\" line, and the core ones get `ticket` and `ready-for-agent`. {"parentUuid":"09354c7b-6de2-4818-9ed0-b04ea0b77bfc","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011CfmifUDUe5huPHZmeXRfK","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01PmyoyUfFpjNoCPyZ1B9EpT","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/tmp/claude-1000/-home-faisa-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/6e0298fd-6441-4373-ab13-28afb21c8981/scratchpad/make_tickets.py","content":"\"\"\"Publish the approved tickets as GitHub issues, blockers first.\"\"\"\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nimport tempfile\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nPARENT = 1\nCORE = [\"ticket\", \"ready-for-agent\"]\nSTRETCH = [\"stretch\"]\n\nTICKETS = [\n    (\"T01\", \"Login, logout and CSRF\", CORE, [],\n     \"An Officer logs in with their email and password, uses the console, and logs out. Passwords are stored only as argon2 hashes. Anonymous visitors never see admin content. Every state-changing form carries a CSRF token. The seed script and `cms create-admin` produce working Admin and Editor Users. The User record already holds email, display name, title, Term, role, active flag and password hash, because later tickets build on it.\",\n     [\n         \"Seeded Admin and Editor log in with email and password and reach the console.\",\n         \"A wrong password and an unknown email get the same generic refusal message, so the form does not reveal which accounts exist.\",\n         \"Logout ends the session, and the same admin URL then redirects to login.\",\n         \"An anonymous request to any admin URL is redirected to login and shows no admin content.\",\n         \"The stored password value is an argon2 hash. A plain password is never stored or logged.\",\n         \"Every state-changing form (including login and logout) carries a CSRF token, and a POST with the token removed is rejected.\",\n         \"Sessions expire after 8 hours, and the signing secret is read from the environment.\",\n         \"The shared logged-in test client fetches the login form's CSRF token before posting, and the existing T00 admin test is updated to log in first, since an anonymous request to the admin page now redirects.\",\n         \"`cms create-admin <email>` asks for a hidden password and creates an Admin, with no default password anywhere in code or demo data.\",\n         \"The seed script creates the Admin and Editor from `.env` values and runs clean with the example values.\",\n     ]),\n    (\"T02\", \"Posts with editor and Preview\", CORE, [\"T01\"],\n     \"An Editor writes a Post in Markdown, saves it as a Draft, previews it, marks it Published, or sets it back to Draft. Editors can change only their own Posts. The Slug and Byline follow the chapter's rules. A simple Posts list lets people reach the editor (filters come in T08).\",\n     [\n         \"An Editor creates a Post with a title and Markdown body, saved as a Draft with the author and created and updated timestamps.\",\n         \"The Slug is generated from the title (lowercase, hyphens), can be edited until the Post is first Published, and a duplicate Slug is refused with a clear error.\",\n         \"Marking a Post Published records the published timestamp, and the Byline (author's full name, title and Term) is copied onto the Post then. Changing the User's title or Term later does not change it.\",\n         \"After first Published the Slug is locked for Editors, and the Admin can unlock it.\",\n         \"An Editor can edit only their own Posts. Requesting another Editor's Post (view, edit or delete) by direct URL is refused. The Admin can edit and delete any Post.\",\n         \"An Editor can set their own Post back to Draft and delete their own Drafts, but cannot delete a Published Post. The Admin can delete any Post.\",\n         \"Editing a Published Post saves in place and it stays Published.\",\n         \"A Preview button next to Save opens a new tab with a \\\"Draft preview, not public\\\" banner, rendered by the same sanitize-then-render code that `cms publish` will use.\",\n         \"In Preview, a body containing `<script>` and an `onerror=` attribute is stripped, basic formatting and links work, and links to other sites get `rel=\\\"noopener\\\"`.\",\n         \"Posts persist across a server restart.\",\n         \"The seed script adds at least one Draft and one Published Post.\",\n     ]),\n    (\"T03\", \"`cms publish`: Posts to a static site\", CORE, [\"T02\"],\n     \"The Admin runs `cms publish` and gets a static site containing only Published Posts, with Home, News and each Post, using relative paths only. It refuses to finish if a Draft would appear.\",\n     [\n         \"`cms publish` writes a Home page showing the 5 latest Published Posts (title, date and first paragraph), a News page listing every Published Post newest-first by published date, and one page per Published Post with its Byline and date.\",\n         \"Only Published Posts appear. A Draft Post's title and Slug appear nowhere in the output.\",\n         \"If a Draft would end up in the output, `cms publish` exits with an error that explains why and does not leave a half-finished site.\",\n         \"Every href and src in the output is relative. There is no `href=\\\"/` or `src=\\\"/` anywhere, and the site works from a subfolder.\",\n         \"Markdown is sanitized in the output. A saved Post containing `<script>` and `onerror=` produces neither in any generated file.\",\n         \"No User email or login name appears anywhere in the output.\",\n         \"A Post set back to Draft is absent from the next render.\",\n         \"The command prints a summary listing every Published item it rendered.\",\n         \"The existing T00 publish tests still pass.\",\n     ]),\n    (\"T04\", \"`cms deploy` and the site live on Pages\", CORE, [\"T03\"],\n     \"The Admin runs `cms deploy`, confirms, and the rendered site is pushed to GitHub Pages, so a Published Post is Live. Deploy stays a separate command from `cms publish`. The README documents the workflow and the handover.\",\n     [\n         \"`cms deploy` is separate from `cms publish`. If the static site does not exist yet, it says to run `cms publish` first.\",\n         \"`cms deploy` asks for confirmation (default no). Answering no pushes nothing and exits cleanly. Answering yes pushes.\",\n         \"Only the static site is pushed. The database, `.env` and secrets are not included.\",\n         \"A successful Deploy records when it happened. A plain password is never stored or logged.\",\n         \"Every state-changing form (including login and logout) carries a CSRF token, and a POST with the token removed is rejected.\",\n         \"Sessions expire after 8 hours, and the signing secret is read from the environment.\",\n         \"The shared logged-in test client fetches the login form's CSRF token before posting, and the existing T00 admin test is updated to log in first, since an anonymous request to the admin page now redirects.\",\n         \"`cms create-admin <email>` asks for a hidden password and creates an Admin, with no default password anywhere in code or demo data.\",\n         \"The seed script creates the Admin and Editor from `.env` values and runs clean with the example values.\",\n     ]),\n    (\"T02\", \"Posts with editor and Preview\", CORE, [\"T01\"],\n     \"An Editor writes a Post in Markdown, saves it as a Draft, previews it, marks it Published, or sets it back to Draft. Editors can change only their own Posts. The Slug and Byline follow the chapter's rules. A simple Posts list lets people reach the editor (filters come in T08).\",\n     [\n         \"An Editor creates a Post with a title and Markdown body, saved as a Draft with the author and created and updated timestamps.\",\n         \"The Slug is generated from the title (lowercase, hyphens), can be edited until the Post is first Published, and a duplicate Slug is refused with a clear error.\",\n         \"Marking a Post Published records the published timestamp, and the Byline (author's full name, title and Term) is copied onto the Post then. Changing the User's title or Term later does not change it.\",\n         \"After first Published the Slug is locked for Editors, and the Admin can unlock it.\",\n         \"An Editor can edit only their own Posts. Requesting another Editor's Post (view, edit or delete) by direct URL is refused. The Admin can edit and delete any Post.\",\n         \"An Editor can set their own Post back to Draft and delete their own Drafts, but cannot delete a Published Post. A declined or failed one does not.\",\n         \"A Published Post is reachable at the GitHub Pages URL over HTTPS, and the `gh-pages` branch has no root-absolute paths.\",\n         \"Tests stub the push, so no test touches `gh-pages`.\",\n         \"The README describes publish-then-deploy and has a handover checklist: the repository, the database and the image folder, with the successor promoted before the outgoing Admin is Deactivated.\",\n     ]),\n    (\"T05\", \"User management, roles and Deactivation\", CORE, [\"T01\"],\n     \"The Admin manages Users: creates them, sets role, title and Term, and Deactivates them when they leave office. Editors are kept out of every admin-only area. A blocked Editor is told whom to ask.\",\n     [\n         \"The Admin creates a User with email, display name, title, Term, role and an initial password, which is stored hashed.\",\n         \"The Admin changes a User's role, title and Term.\",\n         \"The Admin Deactivates a User. Promoting a successor first allows the original Admin to be Deactivated.\",\n         \"An Editor and an anonymous visitor are refused at every user-management URL when requested directly, and the links are hidden from Editors.\",\n         \"An Editor who reaches an admin-only URL sees a message naming the current Admin and a contact line, and the Admin can edit that contact line. The contact line never appears in the static site.\",\n         \"Tests request each admin-only route as Editor and as anonymous and assert a 403 or redirect.\",\n     ]),\n    (\"T06\", \"Temporary passwords and recovery\", CORE, [\"T05\"],\n     \"An Officer who forgot their password can recover without an email server. Cuttable.\",\n     [\n         \"A successful `cms deploy` records a fingerprint of each Published item.\",\n         \"The `cms publish` summary lists only items that are new, changed or removed compared with the last Deploy, instead of every Published item.\",\n         \"The dashboard's Pending release count and the content list's changed marker use the fingerprints.\",\n         \"If content has changed since the last `cms publish`, `cms deploy` warns and stops.\",\n         \"With no previous Deploy, every Published item counts as new.\",\n     ]),\n]\n\n\ndef run(args):\n    r = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, text=True)\n    if r.returncode != 0:\n        sys.exit(f\"FAILED {args[:4]}: {r.stderr}\")\n    return r.stdout.strip()\n\n\nnumbers = {}\nfor tid, title, labels, blockers, build, criteria in TICKETS:\n    if blockers:\n        bl = \"\\n\".join(f\"- {b} (#{numbers[b]})\" for b in blockers)\n    else:\n        bl = \"- None (can start immediately)\"\n    ac = \"\\n\".join(f\"- [ ] {c}\" for c in criteria)\n    body = (f\"## Parent\\n\\nPart of #{PARENT}\\n\\n## What to build\\n\\n{build}\\n\\n\"\n            f\"## Acceptance criteria\\n\\n{ac}\\n\\n## Blocked by\\n\\n{bl}\\n\")\n    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(\"w\", suffix=\".md\", delete=False) as f:\n        f.write(body)\n    cmd = [\"gh\", \"issue\", \"create\", \"--title\", f\"{tid}: {title}\",\n           \"--body-file\", f.name, \"--parent\", str(PARENT)]\n    for l in labels:\n        cmd += [\"--label\", l]\n    url = run(cmd)\n    numbers[tid] = int(url.rstrip(\"/\").split(\"/\")[-1])\n    print(tid, numbers[tid], url)\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"663f6c06-972e-4e85-b290-b83fa61640b0","session_id":"4b1a37e3-ea11-48e9-baa9-b66b752b7a0d","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/faisa/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"6e0298fd-6441-4373-ab13-28afb21c8981","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"4d931cec-365a-4216-b2c6-8f230c59cc3f","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfmin99DBCqZV5JL8mvob","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The 13 tickets are published in dependency order. Each is a sub-issue of spec #1, and the issue numbers are #2 to #14.\n\n| Ticket | Issue | Blocked by |\n|---|---|---|\n| T01 Login, logout and CSRF | #2 | None |\n| T02 Posts with editor and Preview | #3 | T01 |\n| T03 `cms publish`: Posts to a static site | #4 | T02 |\n| T04 `cms deploy` and the site live on Pages | #5 | T03 |\n| T05 User management, roles and Deactivation | #6 | T01 |\n| T06 Temporary passwords and recovery | #7 | T05 |\n| T07 Pages, Assigned editor and Navigation | #8 | T03, T05 |\n| T08 Dashboard and content list | #9 | T02, T04, T07 |\n| T09 Images from the admin-managed folder (stretch) | #10 | T03 |\n| T10 Optional event date on Posts (stretch) | #11 | T02, T03 |\n| T11 `cms backup` (stretch) | #12 | T01 |\n| T12 Login lockout (stretch) | #13 | T01 |\n| T13 Deploy fingerprints (stretch) | #14 | T03, T04 |\n\n- **Labels:** the 8 core tickets have `ticket` and `ready-for-agent`. Each stretch ticket has `stretch` only, as you asked. That means they don't carry `ready-for-agent`, so add it when you decide to build one.\n- **Blocking:** each body has a \"Blocked by\" section, and I also set GitHub's native dependency edges, so the first ticket you can pick up is T01 (#2).\n- **Format:** each ticket has acceptance criteria written to be tested through the two agreed seams.\n\nT01 includes two changes to existing tests:\n- **T00 admin test:** T00's `test_admin_console_answers` expects an anonymous request to `/admin` to return 200. Redirecting anonymous visitors to login breaks that, so T01 updates the test to log in first. It also touches the \"do not delete\" T00 tests, but the change is required by security checklist item 5, so it's deliberate.\n- **`client_as` helper:** the shared helper posts to `/login` with no CSRF token. The spec requires a token on every POST, so T01 changes the helper to fetch the token first.\n\n`.claude/state/phase` is still `tickets`. Start T01 in a fresh session and write `T01` there. I said the community service chair should handle the Community Service page and the alumni relations chair the History page. As president I don't want to be the sole person who can make changes — that's the exact problem we have now with one alum running the old site.\n+- **Q4 — publishing.** Editors can mark their own posts published, but I give final approval: only I run `cms publish`.\n+- **Q5 OVERRIDE (partial) — bylines.** It suggested display name + optional title. I want full name AND title AND the year of their term, because people change positions every year and \"Secretary\" alone would point to the wrong person later.\n+- **Q8 OVERRIDE — images.** It recommended no images this version. I want images: it's a fraternity site and social chairs will want event and service photos.\n+- **Q8 follow-up — how images work.** Claude laid out the risks of real uploads: SVG can carry script, phone photos carry GPS location (the personal-info must-not), and stripping it needs a new dependency (Pillow). Chose (b): an admin-managed image folder, referenced by relative path; only images used by Published content get copied at publish. Tradeoff: I'm the one who adds photos, against my Q1 reason. Uploads = stretch goal.\n+\n+Round 2 (Q9–Q15) — accepted all:\n+- Q9 assigned editors can publish a Page but not delete it; only Admin creates/deletes Pages.\n+- Q10 pages assigned to a person, not a position; deactivating them leaves the page unassigned with a warning. (Means re-assigning by hand every May.)\n+- Q11 byline title + term is a snapshot at first publish, so my term-year idea doesn't rewrite old posts.\n+- Q12 editors see everything but other people's items are read-only — answers my field-note worry about editors deleting each other's posts. No categories/tags/bulk actions; status is a big colored badge (my \"status is hard to see\" note).\n+- Q15 permission wall names the current Admin and a chapter contact — straight from my WordPress note that the error page didn't say who the admin was.\n+- Claude split \"Published\" (editor sets it) from \"Live\" (actually on the site) as two terms in CONTEXT.md.\n+\n+Round 3 (Q16–Q21):\n+- Q16 accepted: editing a Live item changes it in place; \"changed since last release\" marker; my review of the publish summary is the gate.\n+- **Q17 OVERRIDE — event date.** It recommended no event date (write it in the body). {"parentUuid":"283c11c7-b8cb-4855-a6de-bfda5a3d792a","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"a378a176-6e7d-4ec4-be59-4a661caffa35","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /home/faisa/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/.claude/skills/tdd\n\n# Test-Driven Development\n\nTDD is the red → green loop. This skill is the reference that makes that loop produce tests worth keeping: what a good test is, where tests go, the anti-patterns, and the rules of the loop. Every section applies on every cycle: consult them before and during the loop, not after.\n\nWhen exploring the codebase, read `GLOSSARY.md` (if it exists) so test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.\n\n## What a good test is\n\nTests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't. A good test reads like a specification: \"user can checkout with valid cart\" tells you exactly what capability exists, and it survives refactors because it doesn't care about internal structure.\n\nSee [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.\n\n## Seams: where tests go\n\nA **seam** is the public boundary you test at: the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against internals.\n\n**Test only at pre-agreed seams.** Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam. You can't test everything, so agreeing the seams up front is how testing effort lands on the critical paths and complex logic instead of every edge case.\n\nAsk: \"What's the public interface, and which seams should we test?\"\n\nWhen the shape of that interface is itself in question (how deep the module is, where the seam belongs, what the interface should expose), call the Skill tool with \"codebase-design\" for the vocabulary. It is the shared source of the module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage and locality terms, and it is a reference to consult, not a session to run.\n\n## Anti-patterns\n\n- **Implementation-coupled**: mocks internal collaborators, tests private methods, or verifies through a side channel (querying the database instead of using the interface). The tell: the test breaks when you refactor but behavior hasn't changed.\n- **Tautological**: the assertion recomputes the expected value the way the code does (`expect(add(a, b)).toBe(a + b)`, a snapshot derived by hand the same way, a constant asserted equal to itself), so it passes by construction and can never disagree with the code. Expected values must come from an independent source of truth: a known-good literal, a worked example, the spec.\n- **Horizontal slicing**: writing all tests first, then all implementation. Bulk tests verify _imagined_ behavior: you test the _shape_ of things rather than user-facing behavior, the tests go insensitive to real changes, and you commit to test structure before understanding the implementation. Work in **vertical slices** instead: one test → one implementation → repeat, each test a **tracer bullet** that responds to what the last cycle taught you.\n\n## Rules of the loop\n\n- **Red before green.** Write the failing test first, then only enough code to pass it. Don't anticipate future tests or add speculative features.\n- **One slice at a time.** One seam, one test, one minimal implementation per cycle.\n- **Refactoring is not part of the loop.** It belongs to the review stage (see the `code-review` skill), not the red → green implementation cycle.\n"}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"4a0ac950-ee6f-4881-8d9f-d7bf6ef2fffc","timestamp":"2026-10-06T21:56:01.466Z","sourceToolUseID":"toolu_013dg2tPovjeBrtgtWrR7hZt","session_id":"4b1a37e3-ea11-48e9-baa9-b66b752b7a0d","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/faisa/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"6e0298fd-6441-4373-ab13-28afb21c8981","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"160a1d13-f255-45bf-82ee-3755d6c37235","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"a378a176-6e7d-4ec4-be59-4a661caffa35","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01WiqJ9szMWs69Sk6BciGAs8","type":"tool_result","content":"T01: Login, logout and CSRF\n## Parent\n\nPart of #1\n\n## What to build\n\nAn Officer logs in with their email and password, uses the console, and logs out. Passwords are stored only as argon2 hashes. Anonymous visitors never see admin content. Every state-changing form carries a CSRF token. The User record already holds email, display name, title, Term, role, active flag and password hash, because later tickets build on it.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] Seeded Admin and Editor log in with email and password and reach the console.\n- [ ] A wrong password and an unknown email get the same generic refusal message, so the form does not reveal which accounts exist.\n- [ ] Logout ends the session, and the same admin URL then redirects to login.\n- [ ] An anonymous request to any admin URL is redirected to login and shows no admin content.\n- [ ] The stored password value is an argon2 hash. login, logout and CSRF, tested through the HTTP app.\"\"\"\nimport sqlite3\n\nfrom conftest import DEMO_USERS, token_from\n\n\ndef log_in(client, email, password, **extra):\n    token = token_from(client.get(\"/login\").text)\n    return client.post(\"/login\", data={\"email\": email, \"password\": password,\n                                       \"csrf_token\": token, **extra},\n                       follow_redirects=False)\n\n\ndef test_seeded_users_log_in_and_reach_the_console(client_as):\n    for role in (\"admin\", \"editor\"):\n        response = client_as(role).get(\"/admin\")\n        assert response.status_code == 200\n        assert \"hello admin\" in response.text.lower()\n\n\ndef test_wrong_password_and_unknown_email_get_the_same_refusal(client):\n    wrong = log_in(client, DEMO_USERS[\"admin\"][\"email\"], \"not-the-password\")\n    unknown = log_in(client, \"nobody@example.test\", \"not-the-password\")\n    assert wrong.status_code == unknown.status_code == 200\n    assert \"invalid email or password\" in wrong.text.lower()\n    assert \"invalid email or password\" in unknown.text.lower()\n\n\ndef test_failed_login_does_not_start_a_session(client):\n    log_in(client, DEMO_USERS[\"admin\"][\"email\"], \"not-the-password\")\n    assert client.get(\"/admin\", follow_redirects=False).status_code in (302, 303)\n\n\ndef test_anonymous_admin_request_redirects_to_login(client):\n    response = client.get(\"/admin\", follow_redirects=False)\n    assert response.status_code in (302, 303)\n    assert response.headers[\"location\"].endswith(\"/login\")\n    assert \"hello admin\" not in response.text.lower()\n\n\ndef test_logout_ends_the_session(client_as):\n    c = client_as(\"admin\")\n    token = token_from(c.get(\"/admin\").text)\n    out = c.post(\"/logout\", data={\"csrf_token\": token}, follow_redirects=False)\n    assert out.status_code in (302, 303)\n    assert c.get(\"/admin\", follow_redirects=False).status_code in (302, 303)\n\n\ndef test_stored_password_is_an_argon2_hash(db_path):\n    rows = sqlite3.connect(db_path).execute(\n        \"select password_hash from users\").fetchall()\n    assert rows\n    for (value,) in rows:\n        assert value.startswith(\"$argon2\")\n        assert \"test-admin-pw\" not in value and \"test-editor-pw\" not in value\n\n\ndef test_login_without_csrf_token_is_rejected(client):\n    response = client.post(\"/login\", data={\n        \"email\": DEMO_USERS[\"admin\"][\"email\"],\n        \"password\": DEMO_USERS[\"admin\"][\"password\"]}, follow_redirects=False)\n    assert init_db(database: Path) -> None:\n    with connect(database) as conn:\n        conn.execute(_SCHEMA)\n\n\ndef create_user(database: Path, *, email: str, password: str, role: str,\n                display_name: str, title: str = \"\", term: str = \"\") -> int:\n    if role not in ROLES:\n        raise ValueError(f\"role must be one of {ROLES}\")\n    with connect(database) as conn:\n        cur becomes a redirect.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef csrf_token(request: Request) -> str:\n    token = request.session.get(\"csrf\")\n    if not token:\n        token = request.session[\"csrf\"] = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)\n    return token\n\n\nasync def verify_csrf(request: Request) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Dependency for every state-changing route: reject a missing/wrong token.\"\"\"\n    form = await request.form()\n    sent = str(form.get(\"csrf_token\", \"\"))\n    expected = request.session.get(\"csrf\", \"\")\n    if not expected or not secrets.compare_digest(sent, expected):\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail=\"Missing or invalid CSRF token\")\n\n\ndef start_session(request: Request, user_id: int) -> None:\n    request.session.clear()\n    request.session[\"user_id\"] = user_id\n    request.session[\"csrf\"] = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)\n\n\ndef current_user(request: Request):\n    \"\"\"Dependency: the logged-in, active user, or redirect to login.\"\"\"\n    user_id = request.session.get(\"user_id\")\n    user = users.get_user(request.app.state.database, user_id) if user_id else None\n    if user is None or not user[\"is_active\"]:\n        request.session.clear()\n        raise LoginRequired\n    return user\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"e13f0845-29df-43f0-9067-8b75c5605ec0","session_id":"4b1a37e3-ea11-48e9-baa9-b66b752b7a0d","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/faisa/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"6e0298fd-6441-4373-ab13-28afb21c8981","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}
